title: jud-reader-schema-writer-agree: The reader, the JSON Schemas and the writer accept and refuse the same documents
description:
### jud-reader-schema-writer-agree — The reader, the JSON Schemas and the writer accept and refuse the same documents

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | Let `R(d)` = the reader accepts `d`, `S(d)` = the JSON Schema for its kind accepts `d`, and `W(d)` = `to_yaml` of a parsed `d`. Over mutations of every committed document (`examples/jud/*.jud`, `docs` fenced examples): (a) `R(d) => S(d)` and `S(d) => R(d)` except for a named list of cross-checks the schema cannot state (gate vs question primitive, label vs option, `from_turn` vs state shape, policy id not in questions, `part_when` key not in instructions); (b) `R(d) => S(W(d))` and `R(W(d))`; (c) `parse(W(d)) == parse(d)` and the fingerprints are equal. Mutations: delete a key, null a key, duplicate a key, retype a scalar (string/int/float/bool/null/array/object), insert an unknown key at each level, empty each container, swap order, repeat an item, change an `apiVersion`/`kind` byte. |
| **Check** | proptest in `tests/jud.rs` (already has `validator(kind)`, `assert_valid`, `value_of`). The 0.5.1 cluster (eight fixes: 1.1 fields empty/null, schemas accepting what the reader refused, `01` path index, `strict` with no bar, `part_when` emptying a Noul, `apply` of a foreign question, `to_yaml` of an unchecked rubric, supplied option scalars) were each found by review and then pinned with one example; `the_schemas_and_the_parser_refuse_the_same_documents` (`tests/jud.rs:352-362`) is a fixed list of 18. A mutation differential finds the next member of the class. The exception list is part of the test and is reviewed like code. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL on at least the two concrete disagreements found by reading (own entries below: `rubric-reader-refuses-non-wire-scalars` and `rubric-version-number-is-read-as-its-text`); unknown for the rest. Other candidates to look at when it runs: `metadata.version: [1]` or `true` (reader takes any `Value`, `rubric.rs:594-597`; schema allows string or number only); a gate `fallback: 5` (reader `Option<String>` may or may not coerce an int scalar; schema says string); `elapsed_ms: 1.0` (schema `integer` accepts it, serde `u64` may not); a Noul criteria written with bare `true:` (reader maps a YAML bool key, a plain JSON-Schema tool sees a non-string key). |
| **Fault angle** | hostile and hand-edited documents; schema/reader drift when a field is added. |
| **Why it matters** | `.jud` is "a specification other tools implement" (`CLAUDE.md`); a document a validating tool accepts and this reader refuses, or the reverse, forks the format. Eight such bugs in one release is the strongest defect signal in the repo's history. |
| **Priority** | P1: recurring defect class, likely open instances, high blast radius for a published format. |
| **Code anchors** | `tests/jud.rs:77-130`, `:178-362`, `src/jud/rubric.rs:473-515`, `:575-640`, `src/jud/mod.rs:230-245`, `schemas/jud/*.json`, `CHANGELOG.md:517-555` (0.5.1) |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none; a small mutation helper in `tests/support/`. |

**Open Questions:**
- Which cross-checks belong on the exception list? The spec names them (`jud-format.md` Schemas and conformance); the test should derive the list from there.

---

title: base-url-userinfo-and-scheme-are-refused-or-neutralised: No credential in the base URL overrides the key or reaches logs; no unusable base URL survives `build`
description:
### base-url-userinfo-and-scheme-are-refused-or-neutralised — No credential in the base URL overrides the key or reaches logs; no unusable base URL survives `build`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For `base_url("https://user:pw@host/api")`: the request carries `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (never Basic), and no `Debug`, `Display` or span field of the `Client`, `ClientBuilder` or any `Error` contains `pw`. For a base URL whose scheme is not `http`/`https`, or which cannot be a base (`mailto:x`, `data:`), `build()` returns `Error::Url`, never an `Ok` client whose every call fails later (and, for a non-http scheme, is retried). |
| **Check** | wiremock test in `tests/client.rs` (settles bead `judgment-hle`): `base_url(server.uri().replace("http://", "http://u:p@"))`, read the received `authorization` header; assert it equals `Bearer key`. Then `format!("{:?}")` of builder and client and of an `Err(Transport)` from a refused port, assert no `p`-secret substring (use a distinctive secret). Second test: `build()` for `ftp://h`, `mailto:a@b`, `file:///x`; time the failing call with default retries to show the wasted backoff if it builds. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL on the Debug and scheme parts, unknown on the Basic part. `build` keeps userinfo in `base_url` (`client.rs:452-459`), and `Client`'s `Debug` prints `self.base_url.as_str()` (`client.rs:504-512`) so the password is printed raw, while the api key is carefully redacted. `ClientBuilder`'s Debug prints the raw `base_url` string (`client.rs:347-358`). Whether a URL userinfo beats a default `Authorization` header in reqwest is read from reqwest's source by the tracker (`judgment-hle`), not run. Scheme: `build` never checks it (`:450-475`); reqwest reports an unsupported scheme as a builder error at `send`, which `TransportRetry::Any` retries (`http.rs:381-392`, `:192-198`). A cannot-be-a-base URL is accepted by `Url::parse`, `set_path` is a no-op for it, and the first `join` fails with `Error::Url`. |
| **Fault angle** | misconfigured base URL; proxy-style URLs with credentials. |
| **Why it matters** | Credential handling (the repo's one secret rule) and a wrong-account call if Basic wins. Bead `judgment-hle`. |
| **Priority** | P1: credential leak into logs is near certain by reading (`Debug`), and the auth precedence is an open credential-handling bug. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/client.rs:347-358`, `:450-475`, `:504-512`, `src/http.rs:192-198`, `:381-392` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Does reqwest 0.13 let userinfo override a default `Authorization` header? One wiremock request settles it.
- Does `reqwest::Error` Display include the URL with userinfo? Run a refused-port call with a userinfo base URL.

---

## Run result (executed in an isolated worktree at 56acead)
Server received `Authorization: Basic dXU6UFdTRUNSRVQ=` instead of the Bearer key for base URL http://uu:PWSECRET@host; `{:?}` of Client and ClientBuilder prints the password (key redacted). tests/invest.rs c1_userinfo.

## Merged duplicate: base-url-userinfo-bearer-precedence — A base URL with userinfo never replaces the Bearer key silently (judgment-hle)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any base URL with a username and/or password, either `ClientBuilder::build` returns `Err`, or every request's `Authorization` header equals `Bearer <key>`. |
| **Check** | wiremock test in `tests/client.rs`: base URLs `http://user:pw@HOST`, `http://user@HOST`, `http://:pw@HOST`, percent-encoded userinfo, with a mock matching `header("authorization", "Bearer test-key")` and `.expect(1)`; also `list_models` (same `make` path). proptest over userinfo strings is optional; four spellings cover the mechanism. Wire-level because the bug is a precedence rule inside reqwest. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL (settled by reading, not run). `build` keeps the userinfo in `base_url` (`client.rs:452-459`) and puts the Bearer in the client-level `default_headers` (`client.rs:470-478`). reqwest 0.13.5 `RequestBuilder::new` (`async_impl/request.rs:172-186`) strips the userinfo from the URL and appends a sensitive `Authorization: Basic` header; `execute_request` (`async_impl/client.rs:2633-2637`) only inserts a default header when the key is vacant. So the key is never sent and the URL's password is. The existing test pins this as intended: `tests/jud_record.rs:1173-1176` comment "Userinfo in the URL is sent as Basic credentials, in place of the key's Bearer header, so this server accepts any authorization"; fixing it changes that test. |
| **Fault angle** | Environment/config: `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` copied from a tool that embeds credentials (`https://user:token@gateway/`). |
| **Why it matters** | Silent wrong credentials: the gateway's userinfo goes where the TypeSafe key was meant, the key is dropped, and the run gets a 401 or, worse, an anonymous success on a permissive local server. Bead `judgment-hle` (confirmed by mechanism). |
| **Priority** | P2: known defect with a clear fix (refuse or strip userinfo and set Basic explicitly); credential misdirection, not exposure. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/client.rs:452-459,470-478`, reqwest `src/async_impl/request.rs:172-186,590-605`, `src/async_impl/client.rs:2633-2637`, `tests/jud_record.rs:1168-1260` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Intended behaviour: refuse at `build` (`Error::Url`), strip, or honour as Basic for gateways that need it? The property is stated as "either/or" so it survives the choice; the old pinned test must change with it.

---

Evidence:
- Read reqwest 0.13.5 `async_impl/request.rs:172-186` (`RequestBuilder::new` strips userinfo via `extract_authority` and calls `basic_auth` -> `header_sensitive`), `async_impl/client.rs:2633-2637` (default headers inserted only if `Entry::Vacant`). That settles the open question O2 of agent C by reading.
- `tests/jud_record.rs:1173-1176` states the Basic-in-place-of-Bearer outcome as accepted; therefore a fix is a behaviour change.
- reqwest strips the userinfo from the URL before building errors, so `Error::Transport` Display does not leak it (matches the passing test at `jud_record.rs:1236-1259`).
- Not run.

## Merged duplicate: base-url-secrets-never-printed — No command or Debug impl prints the raw base URL

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For a base URL carrying userinfo, a query token and a fragment, none of `format!("{client:?}")`, `format!("{builder:?}")`, `jud config` stdout, `jud record --dry-run` stdout/stderr, nor any stderr line of `jud RUBRIC` / `eval` / `tune` contains the userinfo, the query or the fragment. |
| **Check** | Unit tests in `src/client.rs` tests for the two Debug impls (extend `debug_output_redacts_the_key`, line 1508) with base `https://u:s3cret@h/p?key=abc#frag`; CLI subprocess tests in `tests/jud_cli.rs` (`config`) and `tests/jud_record.rs` (`--dry-run`, which needs no server) using the same canaries and `assert!(!text.contains("s3cret"))`. Existing coverage: only `record` run and failure messages (`tests/jud_record.rs:1168-1260`), never `config`, `--dry-run` or Debug. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL on four sinks: `ClientBuilder` Debug prints `self.base_url` (`client.rs:350`), `Client` Debug prints `base_url.as_str()` (`client.rs:507`, userinfo kept by `Url::join`), `describe_plan` prints `plain(p.base_url)` of the raw `resolved.base_url()` (`record.rs:264`, built at `record.rs:218`), and `jud config` serialises `Resolved.base_url` raw (`config.rs:70`, `show` at `:225`). Latent: `Resolved` and `File` derive `Debug` with a plain `api_key_value` / `api_key` (`config.rs:66,38`); no `{:?}` of them exists today (grep `{:?}` in `bin/jud` finds none), so this is a landmine, not a leak. |
| **Fault angle** | Environment (`TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` with credentials or a signed-URL token), then a shared terminal or CI log. |
| **Why it matters** | Same secret classes `public_url` was written for, on the sinks that were missed. `--dry-run` is the command people paste into issues. |
| **Priority** | P2: credential exposure in common diagnostic output; small fix (`public_url` at the four sites). |
| **Code anchors** | `src/client.rs:350,507`, `src/bin/jud/record.rs:218,264`, `src/bin/jud/config.rs:38,66,70,225-230`, `src/bin/jud/backend.rs:123,161,177,188` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- `jud config` is documented as "the resolved backend as JSON, the key never shown" (`config.rs:224`): is a raw `base_url` there deliberate (so a person can see exactly what is configured)? If so print a `base_url` without secrets plus a boolean `base_url_has_credentials`.
- A static test (grep for `derive(Debug` on any struct holding `api_key`) would pin the latent `Resolved`/`File` Debug case; not decided whether that belongs in the property.

---

Evidence:
- Read `ClientBuilder`/`Client` Debug (`client.rs:340-358,505-512`), `config.rs` `Resolved` (derives Debug, Serialize; `base_url` plain), `describe_plan` (`record.rs:243-285`), `backend.rs:188-197`.
- `grep -n '{:?}' bin/jud/{backend,config,record,main}.rs`: no Debug print of `Resolved`/`File` (latent only).
- Existing tests: `tests/jud_record.rs:1168-1260`, `tests/jud_tune.rs:1647-1668`; none for `config`, `--dry-run`, Debug.
- Not run.

title: recorder-write-crash-poisons-directory: Library recording writer is not crash-safe and one torn file makes `Replay::open` refuse the directory
description:
### recorder-write-crash-poisons-directory — Library recording writer is not crash-safe and one torn file makes `Replay::open` refuse the directory

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For every prefix length k of the bytes `write_recording` would write, if the write stops after k bytes, `Replay::open(dir)` still succeeds and still answers every other recording in the directory, and a recording the caller paid for is either fully readable or absent. |
| **Check** | Integration test in `tests/backend.rs` using the RLIMIT_FSIZE shim above, or a unit test with a failing `Write` once a seam exists. Parent process: Recorder over a `Fake` writes recordings A, B, C into a dir. Child (test binary re-exec with an env var) writes recording D under `ulimit -f` swept over sizes below `len(D)`. After each child, parent asserts `Replay::open(dir)` is `Ok` and A, B, C replay. A proptest-style sweep over k is cheap. Assert also that a successful D is byte-identical to `serde_json::to_string_pretty` plus newline. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. `src/eval/mod.rs:175` is `std::fs::write(&path, text + "\n")` (truncate in place, no temp, no fsync); `Replay::open` returns `InvalidRecording` for the first unparsable `.json` (`src/backend.rs:451-459`, `?`), so one torn `<hash>.json` makes the whole directory unreadable until a human deletes it. |
| **Fault angle** | Process kill or ENOSPC between truncate and the last byte; full disk; power loss (no `sync_all`, no directory fsync). |
| **Why it matters** | The recording is a paid model response (money) and the directory is shared by every test that replays it; the failure is loud but total. `jud record` was given an atomic writer for exactly this (decision 0021, `record.rs:600-632`); the library writer still has the original bug. beads `3zp` (per sut/d, `tune.rs:138` bead) covers `tune`; the library writer is wider than that bead. |
| **Priority** | P1: data loss of paid answers plus a whole-directory outage from one crash, in the crate's default recording path. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/eval/mod.rs:162-181`; `src/backend.rs:361-396`, `:417-470`; `src/bin/jud/record.rs:620-632` (the pattern to reuse) |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none for the RLIMIT shim; a `write_recording` that takes a temp-then-rename helper shared with the CLI would make a fix testable once |

**Open Questions:**
- When the write fails, `Recorder::answer` returns `Err(Error::Io)` and drops the response it already paid for (`backend.rs:385-392`; no await between `inner.answer` and the write, so cancellation cannot land there, only a write error can). Should the error carry the response, or should the write failure be an `Observer` event and the answer returned? Unknown whether callers want recording to be best effort.
- Should `Replay::open` skip (and report) an unparsable `.json` instead of failing the directory? CHANGELOG (line ~237) says refusing is intended; the property above holds either way once writers are atomic.

---

## Run result (executed in an isolated worktree at 56acead)
Under `ulimit -f 2` with SIGXFSZ ignored, Recorder::answer returned Err(Io, File too large) and left a 1024-byte truncated .json; Replay::open(dir) then failed with InvalidRecording ('EOF while parsing a string') for the whole directory.

## Merged duplicate: library-recorder-write-is-atomic — A concurrent reader or a failed write never sees a torn recording from `Recorder`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | While any number of threads call `Recorder::answer` (or `eval::write_recording`) for the same and for different requests into one directory, a concurrent `Replay::open` of that directory never returns `InvalidRecording`; and when a write fails partway (file-size limit), no file under a final recording name holds partial bytes. |
| **Check** | Two tests in `tests/backend.rs` (std threads, tempdir). (1) Concurrency: a writer thread calls `write_recording` 300 times with a recording whose `response.extra` carries ~2 MiB so the truncate-then-write window is wide; a reader thread loops `Replay::open(dir)`; assert no `Err`. (2) Fault shim, no unsafe: run the test body in a child process launched through `sh -c 'ulimit -f 4; trap "" XFSZ; exec <test-binary> --exact child_write'` so `write` returns `EFBIG` after a partial write; the child calls `write_recording`, then the parent runs `Replay::open` and asserts no torn `.json`. Std threads and a child process fit better than loom: the race is with the filesystem, not with memory. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL: `write_recording` is `create_dir_all` then `std::fs::write(&path, text + "\n")` (`eval/mod.rs:175`), a truncate-in-place at the final name; `Replay::open` returns the first parse error with `?` (`backend.rs` `open`, the `Some("json")` arm), so one torn file hides every recording in the directory. Contrast `jud record`'s temp-file-and-rename (`record.rs:620-632`). The `ulimit -f` variant leaves the truncated file permanently. Probabilistic for (1); (2) deterministic. |
| **Fault angle** | concurrent reader/writer, ENOSPC/EFBIG mid-write, kill mid-write |
| **Why it matters** | Recordings are the offline test fixtures the crate sells ("record and replay"); a half-written fixture fails `Replay::open` for the whole suite, with `InvalidRecording` pointing at a file that is merely torn. Also affects two test processes recording into one directory. |
| **Priority** | P2: confirmed by code, loud (not silent) failure, library path only |
| **Code anchors** | `src/eval/mod.rs:162-181` (write at `:175`); `src/backend.rs:371-389` (Recorder), `:440-475` (`open` with `?`); `src/bin/jud/record.rs:620-632` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none for (1); a `--exact` child test entry and `sh` for (2) |

**Open Questions:**
- `Recorder::answer` returns `Err(Error::Io)` when the write fails, discarding the billed response the inner backend just returned (`backend.rs:385-388`). Intended (a recorder that cannot record has failed) or should it return the response with a warning? `(needs human input)`
- Should `Replay::open` skip or report-and-continue past one unreadable `.json`, as opposed to failing the directory? Documented behaviour for hand-edited files is "fails naming the question". `(needs human input)`

---

## Merged duplicate: recorder-concurrent-writers-tear-a-file — Two concurrent identical requests, or a reader during a write, see a torn recording

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | With N threads each calling `Recorder::answer` for the same request (same `<hash>.json`) and one thread repeatedly calling `Replay::open(dir)`, every `open` succeeds and every final file parses to one writer's complete recording. |
| **Check** | `tokio` multi-thread or `std::thread` stress test in `tests/backend.rs`: a `Fake` whose responses differ in length (vary the request id or `elapsed_ms` digits) behind `Recorder`, 8 writers x 2000 iterations on one directory, plus a reader loop; assert no `InvalidRecording`. This is a stress test, not loom: the race is in the kernel's `O_TRUNC` + `write` ordering, outside what loom models. Failure is probabilistic, so run in a loop with a bounded time budget and report the first torn bytes. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL (probabilistically). `fs::write` = open(O_TRUNC) then write: A truncates, B truncates, A writes N bytes, B writes M<N bytes: the file is B's text plus the tail of A's, which `serde_json::from_str` rejects as trailing characters; a reader between truncate and write sees an empty file. `src/eval/mod.rs:175`, no lock, no temp. |
| **Fault angle** | In-process concurrency over a shared `&dyn SystemOne`; two processes on one directory. |
| **Why it matters** | Same outage as the crash case but reachable without any fault: a service sharing a Recorder across tasks, or `cargo test` running two tests on one directory. |
| **Priority** | P2: narrow race window but no fault needed; fixed by the same atomic writer as the crash case. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/eval/mod.rs:162-181`; `src/backend.rs:361-396` (no lock around the write); `src/backend.rs:417-470` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none (a barrier inside the writer would make it deterministic but is not required) |

**Open Questions:**
- None

---

title: rubric-lowering-and-apply-are-total-for-every-accepted-rubric: What the reader accepts always lowers or fails typed, and the request is answerable
description:
### rubric-lowering-and-apply-are-total-for-every-accepted-rubric — What the reader accepts always lowers or fails typed, and the request is answerable

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any rubric `Rubric::parse` accepts, any state and any supplied options: `Rubric::lower` returns `Ok` or a typed `jud::Error` and never panics; on `Ok` the questions are exactly those whose `when` holds, in the rubric's order, each Choice with `options_from: request` offers the supplied options in the order supplied and then its static ones, and the request passes the builder's own checks; a `Fake` scripted for the asked ids answers it, `Response::verify` accepts, and `Rubric::apply` returns one verdict per asked question in wire order and none for a question left out by `when`; lowering the same inputs twice gives identical bytes. |
| **Check** | proptest (H1) in `tests/jud.rs` (the target already builds rubrics from text and has the schema validator). Generator: rubrics written as YAML text (1 to 5 questions of the three primitives, `when` and `part_when` paths into a generated state vocabulary with objects, arrays, `null` and absent keys, `options_from: request` with 0 to 3 static options), states from the same vocabulary, supplied options 0 to 4 per question including an option under a key already offered. title: validation-error-echo-of-state-is-not-quoted: A server that echoes the state in a validation error does not get it into a message
description:
### validation-error-echo-of-state-is-not-quoted — A server that echoes the state in a validation error does not get it into a message

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For a 400, 413 or 422 whose body echoes a piece of the request state (a FastAPI-style `detail` list whose entries carry `input` and `ctx`, an object `detail`, a plain-text body, a body with `message` holding the state), no `Error` Display or Debug and no CLI stderr line contains the state canary; the documented exception is the raw-body fallback, whose acceptance is decided by HD11. |
| **Check** | wiremock test in `tests/client.rs` (and one CLI line in `tests/jud_record.rs`): state `{"note": "CANARY-STATE-7c1"}`; the responder returns four bodies: (a) `{"detail":[{"loc":["body","state"],"msg":"bad","type":"x","input":"CANARY-STATE-7c1","ctx":{"v":"CANARY-STATE-7c1"}}]}`; (b) the same entry with no `msg`; (c) `{"detail":{"input":"CANARY-STATE-7c1"}}`; (d) the raw text `invalid: CANARY-STATE-7c1`. Assert with the H8 scanner on `err.to_string()`, `format!("{err:?}")` and, for the CLI, stderr. Table test, not proptest: the shapes are the four ways `error_detail` can reach (or miss) its message arm. |
| **Expected today** | (a) passes: `validation_issue` reads `loc`, `msg` and `type` only (`src/client.rs:845-868`). (b), (c), (d) EXPECTED TO FAIL: an entry without a string `msg` is dropped, no `message`, `error` or issue message results, and `error_detail` falls through to `.unwrap_or_else(\|\| body.to_owned())` (`src/client.rs:831`), which `http::truncate`s to 2,000 bytes and quotes. That fallback is documented ("then the raw body, truncated to 2,000 bytes", `docs/project/internals.md:39`), so (b) to (d) are a design question, not a slip. |
| **Fault angle** | A server or gateway that reflects the request into its error text; a misconfigured validator that omits `msg`; a proxy error page that echoes the body. |
| **Why it matters** | `state` is the application's data (a ticket, a customer message); the crate's own docs say a validation issue's `input` "can echo a piece of the state" and so is never read, and the reader module says the same of messages "that land in a log" (`src/jud/mod.rs:304-310`). The guarantee holds for one body shape and leaks for the neighbouring ones, where the leak lands in CI logs and in `jud record`'s stopped-at line. No existing test places a canary in `input` (`grep '"input"' tests/client.rs` is empty). |
| **Priority** | P2: privacy of application data in logs; one shape already guarded, so the expected fix is small. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/client.rs:790-868` (`error_detail`, `validation_issue`), `:713-760` (`classify`), `src/http.rs:466-479` (`truncate`), `src/error.rs:79-145` (variants that interpolate `detail`), `docs/project/internals.md:39` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | H8 (scanner); none in `src/` |

**Open Questions:**
- Is quoting the raw body when no message can be read intended to stay (it is the Python SDK's order)? If yes the property narrows to (a) and the check documents that (b) to (d) quote the body. `(needs human input: HD11)`
- Should the fallback print the body only when it contains no echo of the state, which the client cannot know without the state? The client holds the state in `Request`, so a substring check is possible but is a new behaviour.

| **Type** | Safety |

| **Check** | Differential. Library test in a new `tests/calibration_differential.rs`: proptest generates up to 30 labelled answers with confidences on the two-decimal grid (ties at 0.05 steps are common), Score distributions that are spread (peak 0.4 on level 0, mass on 2) and single-peaked ones; run `Judgment::of_answer` through `gate_table` and `Rubric::apply` through a re-implemented `policy_is_right`. Split in three subproperties: (a) Choice, non-strict (positive control, expected to pass); (b) strict, with confidences placed exactly at the bar; (c) Score, spread distributions. ### eval-ece-uses-wire-confidence-not-answer-probability — Reported calibration error measures the server's concentration statistic

| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any set of labelled Choice or Score answers, the `ece`, `confidence_when_right` and `confidence_when_wrong` that `jud eval` reports equal `expected_calibration_error` over `(probability of the predicted option or level, correct)`, as `examples/typed_decisions.rs:187-210` defines calibration; a model whose stated probabilities are exactly right (a 3-option Choice at (0.6, 0.2, 0.2), right 60% of the time) reports ECE close to 0 for Choice, Score and Noul alike. |
| **Check** | Unit test next to `QuestionMetrics::summarise` (`src/eval/mod.rs`) plus one CLI case in `tests/jud_eval.rs`. Build 100 `Answer::Choice` values with `probabilities {a:0.6,b:0.2,c:0.2}`, hosted-shaped `confidence 0.40` (the formula in `answer.rs:666`), label `a` on 60 of them. Assert `ECE < 0.02`. Today it is 0.20. Add the Noul twin (p=0.6, right 60%) and assert that Noul and Choice ECE agree for the same underlying calibration. A proptest generates a categorical distribution, labels in exact proportion, and compares `of_answer`'s ECE with the example's. A pure function over small inputs, so a unit or proptest fits, not wiremock. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL for Choice and Score. `Judgment::of_answer` copies the server's `confidence` (`src/eval/mod.rs:352-358` for Choice, `:379` for Score); only a Noul uses `max(p,1-p)` (`:314-325`). The existing tests pin the wire-confidence numbers (`tests/jud_eval.rs:187`), so fixing it changes pinned figures and is a decision, not a drive-by. |
| **Fault angle** | A server whose `confidence` field is defined differently (TypeSafe: `(p_max-1/n)/(1-1/n)`; Laya: one minus normalised entropy; `answer.rs:660-665`); the OpenRouter and hosted paths differ again. |
| **Why it matters** | `jud eval` prints "calibration error" next to accuracy, and `docs/project/verification/laya-typed-decisions.md:101` says calibration is graded on the answer's probability "not on the wire's confidence field". The CLI does the opposite, so its ECE is not comparable across questions of different primitive or across servers, and a well-calibrated model can look 20 points off. The gate itself must still use the wire confidence (the policy compares it, `rubric.rs:756`), so only the reported metric is affected. Blast radius: silent wrong figure in a report that people tune bars from. |
| **Priority** | P1 (silent wrong number in the headline calibration metric; the crate's own example says the CLI path is wrong) |
| **Code anchors** | `src/eval/mod.rs:314-325,333-390,413-460`; `src/eval/metrics.rs:28-50`; `src/answer.rs:660-690,787-812`; `examples/typed_decisions.rs:187-210`; `src/bin/jud/eval.rs:472` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none (a `Judgment` constructor that grades on `p(predicted)` is the fix, not the check) |

**Open Questions:**
- Is the intended fix a second confidence field on `Judgment` (wire for gates, probability for ECE), or relabelling the metric? The decision decides which pinned test numbers move.

title: untrusted-document-errors-quote-nothing: Errors from reading a rubric, cases or recording file never contain a value from the document
description:
### untrusted-document-errors-quote-nothing — Errors from reading a rubric, cases or recording file never contain a value from the document

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any `.jud` document or `.json` recording that fails to read, the error text (`Error::to_string()`, and the `jud check` / `Replay::open` message) contains no string value, key name or number taken from the document body beyond line/column and field paths the format itself defines. |
| **Check** | Integration test in `tests/jud.rs` (the existing `a_syntax_error_quotes_no_part_of_the_document`, line 397, covers the YAML syntax stage only). Generate documents of each kind with a canary `TOPSECRET-4411` placed in: a wrong-typed `spec.elapsed_ms`, a `spec.response.answers.<q>.noul` string, an unknown field name inside `spec`, an unknown key under a rubric question, a wrong-typed `expect`, a state value; parse via `Rubric::parse`, `Cases::parse`, `parse_recording`, `Replay::open` on a `.json` file; assert the canary is absent from the error. A proptest over where the canary lands (path into a valid document, replaced by a canary of the wrong type) would find more sinks than a table; recommended. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL for the recording paths (read, not run). `parse_recording` maps `serde_json::from_value` errors with `e.to_string()` into `Error::Invalid.reason` (`jud/mod.rs:273-276`); serde's `invalid type: string "TOPSECRET-4411", expected u64` and `unknown field `TOPSECRET`` quote the value. `Replay::open` does the same for `.json` (`backend.rs:446-463` `reason: source.to_string()`). Rubric/cases go through `serde_saphyr` with no snippet; whether its type errors quote scalars is unknown. `Error::Case { reason: e.to_string() }` (`cases.rs:257-260`) wraps another error. The doc comment promises "An error ... quotes nothing, because a document's state can be someone's data and the message lands in a log" (`jud/mod.rs:304-310`). |
| **Fault angle** | Hostile or hand-edited recording/rubric from a PR (T2); state data in cases that is customer data. |
| **Why it matters** | `state` can hold customer data and recordings hold model output; both end up in CI logs on a validation failure. Also unbounded: serde prints the whole offending string, so one 8 MiB string becomes an 8 MiB error line. |
| **Priority** | P2: privacy/log hygiene on a stated guarantee; narrow fix (map serde errors to a path-only message). |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/mod.rs:247-277,304-319`, `src/backend.rs:446-452`, `src/jud/cases.rs:255-262`, `tests/jud.rs:393-405` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Does serde-saphyr's own type-error text quote scalars for rubric/cases? Settled by running the table, not by reading.

---

## Evidence trail
- Read `parse_recording`, `from_text`, `cases.rs:255-262`, `Replay::open` JSON branch. `tests/jud.rs:393-405` covers syntax errors only.
- serde's `invalid_type` Display (`invalid type: string "x", expected u64`) is known behaviour, not executed here.
- Not verified: serde-saphyr message text for typed rubric/cases fields.

## Merged duplicate: jud-errors-quote-no-document-text — A reader error holds no unbounded or unescaped text from the document

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any document, `jud::Error`'s `Display` is at most 512 bytes and contains no control character, bidi override or newline taken from the document, at every variant: `Version.found`, `Kind.found`, `Invalid.field` from an unknown top-level key, the Noul criteria key, `options_from`, `part_when` names, state paths, `Case.reason`. `Syntax` already quotes nothing. |
| **Check** | proptest in `tests/jud.rs`: put one hostile string (4 KB, `\n`, `\x1b[31m`, `\u{202E}`) at each echo site of a valid skeleton and assert the two bounds on `to_string()`. Sites are enumerable by grep for `{other}`, `found:`, `key.clone()` in `src/jud/`. Existing coverage: `a_syntax_error_quotes_no_part_of_the_document` (`tests/jud.rs:397-405`) for `Syntax` only. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL at several sites: `Error::Kind { found }` is the raw `kind` string (`mod.rs:177`), `Error::Version { found }` is `other.to_string()` of the whole `apiVersion` value (`mod.rs:169`, unbounded for a long scalar or a big mapping), the top-level-key refusal puts the raw key in `field` (`mod.rs:236-241`), the Noul criteria error prints `{other}` raw (`rubric.rs:395`), the `options_from` error prints `{other}` (`rubric.rs:459-461`), `check_path` prints the raw path (`mod.rs:397-405`). Only `check_name` escapes and cuts through `sanitize_server_str` (`mod.rs:324-335`). The CLI's `out::plain` (`src/bin/jud/out.rs:46`) escapes C0 controls but not length or bidi, so the CLI inherits the gap. The docs justify quoting nothing "because a document's state can be someone's data and the message lands in a log"; the echoed sites are keys and enums, not state, so the real exposure is log injection and unbounded messages, not data leaks. |
| **Fault angle** | hostile or malformed documents. |
| **Why it matters** | A 10 MB `apiVersion` or a key with ANSI escapes ends up in a log or on a terminal. Also keeps the doc's stated rule true. |
| **Priority** | P3: the author controls the document; impact is hygiene. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/mod.rs:166-193`, `:230-245`, `:324-335`, `:397-405`, `src/jud/rubric.rs:392-397`, `:456-463`, `src/bin/jud/out.rs:43-50` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

- Is `Kind`/`Version` quoting intended to be unbounded ("refused by name")? A cut at 64 chars would keep the name useful.

description:
### blank-or-undecodable-env-is-refused-not-skipped — A set but unusable `TYPESAFE_*` / `JUD_REPLAY` never silently selects another server, key or mode

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For each variable V in {TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, JUD_REPLAY} and each value in {unset, "", "   ", non-UTF-8 bytes}: unset behaves as today; every other value either exits 2 naming V before any network call, or is documented as equal to unset and says so on stderr; in particular a base URL that does not come from the environment is never the hosted default while the variable is set. |
| **Check** | CLI subprocess test in `tests/jud_cli.rs` (the `jud()` helper there already pins `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; extend with `OsString` values via `Command::env`, non-UTF-8 through `std::os::unix::ffi::OsStringExt`). Cases: (a) `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=""`/`" "`/`\xff` with a config file naming a mock and with none: assert `jud config` and `jud RUBRIC` do not report `base_url_from` `default`/`config_file` silently; (b) `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` blank with a different key in the config file: assert the file's key is not used; (c) `JUD_REPLAY=""` for every command (`jud`, `eval`, `tune`, `check`) gives the same exit status as unset. Subprocess because env resolution is process-wide. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL for all three. `env_var` is `std::env::var(name).ok().filter(non-blank)` (`config.rs:122-124`): blank, whitespace and `NotUnicode` all become `None`, so `resolve` (`config.rs:127-152`) falls to the config file and then to `DEFAULT_BASE_URL`. No test passes a blank or non-UTF-8 value (`grep -n 'blank\|OsStr' tests/jud_cli.rs` finds none relevant). |
| **Fault angle** | Environment: CI secret that expanded to empty (`TYPESAFE_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.X }}` unset), a shell `export TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=`, a non-UTF-8 byte from a locale. |

description:
### public-url-strips-every-spelling — `public_url` agrees with a real URL parser about what is userinfo, query and fragment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For every string `u` that `url::Url::parse` accepts, `public_url(u)` contains none of `parsed.username()`, `parsed.password()`, `parsed.query()`, `parsed.fragment()` (when non-empty), and is idempotent. |
| **Check** | proptest (add as dev-dependency) in `src/bin/jud/backend.rs` tests: generate scheme in {http, https}, 0-3 slashes or backslashes after the colon, optional userinfo from an alphabet including `@ : / ? # \ %40 tab`, host, port, path, query, fragment; oracle is `Url::parse` (reqwest re-exports `Url`; the `url` crate is already in the tree). Differential, because a hand-rolled `split_once("://")` is exactly what the WHATWG algorithm disagrees with. Seed the generator with the known counterexamples below so it fails deterministically. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL (by reading `backend.rs:188-197` against the WHATWG special-scheme rules; one proptest line settles it). `public_url("https:user:tok@host/")` has no `://` so it is returned whole (`:189-191`); `https:///user:tok@host/` parses as host `host` with userinfo `user:tok` but `public_url` takes an empty authority and keeps `/user:tok@host/` as the "path"; backslash forms (`https:\\user:tok@host`) likewise. The unit test pins only three well-formed spellings (`backend.rs:204-215`). |
| **Fault angle** | Environment/config strings and, through `recorded_server`, a `server:` field read from an untrusted recording (`tune.rs:700-722`) that is then written into a committed tuned rubric. |
| **Why it matters** | `public_url` is the single gate between a credentialed URL and files meant to be committed (recordings' `server`, tuning provenance) and messages (`announce`). Any bypass defeats the gate everywhere at once. |
| **Priority** | P2: single chokepoint, likely bypass, cheap to fix (parse with `Url`, clear userinfo/query/fragment, fall back to a fixed placeholder when unparsable instead of echoing). |
| **Code anchors** | `src/bin/jud/backend.rs:188-197`, `src/bin/jud/backend.rs:200-216`, `src/bin/jud/tune.rs:700-722`, `src/bin/jud/backend.rs:177` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none (`public_url` is a pure `&str -> String`; add `url` as an explicit dev-dependency of the bin tests if `reqwest::Url` is not reachable without the `http` feature). |

**Open Questions:**
- "A string that is not a URL is returned as it is" (`backend.rs:186`): should an unparsable string be echoed at all (it can be `user:pass@host`, which `Url::parse` reads as scheme `user`)? Proposed: print `<invalid URL>`.

The CLI forwards `{e}` unescaped: `backend.rs:127` then `Failure::report` -> `out::line` (`out.rs:16`) with no `plain`. The docs claim otherwise: `docs/project/internals.md:86` "Every server-chosen string that can reach a message ... goes through one bound". Existing tests (`tests/jud_eval.rs:1208`, `tests/jud_tune.rs:1710`) cover model names only. |
| **Fault angle** | Hostile or broken server, captive portal or proxy HTML page; a body with ANSI/OSC sequences and `::error::` / `::set-env` workflow commands (the tune test already uses `::error::spoofed` as its canary). |

- Whether `ErrorBody::kind` and `ValidationIssue::{loc,msg,kind}` (all server strings, unbounded within the 8 MiB body) should be bounded too.

title: server-echoed-key-never-surfaces: A server that echoes the Authorization header cannot get the key into any output
description:
### server-echoed-key-never-surfaces — A server that echoes the Authorization header cannot get the key into any output

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any key K and any server reply that contains K (verbatim, or as `Bearer K`) in an error body, an error JSON field, a 2xx `extra` field, a header or a body `id`, no `Error` Display, `Error` Debug, tracing event or span field, or `.jud` / `.json` recording written from it contains K. |
| **Check** | wiremock test in `tests/client.rs` with a `Respond` closure that reads the received `authorization` header and splices it into: a 400/403/402/500 body (string, `{"error":{"message":..}}`, `{"detail":[{"msg":..}]}`), a 2xx `extra` field and a 2xx body `id`. Assert `!format!("{err}")`, `!format!("{err:?}")` contain K, and the capture layer in `tests/spans.rs` (existing `Captured`) holds no K in any event or field. A second CLI subprocess test (`tests/jud_record.rs`, same shape as `credentials_in_the_base_url_reach_neither_a_recording_nor_a_message`, line 1168) runs `jud record` against the same mock and greps stderr and every file under `--out` for K. A table-driven test is enough (finite set of echo positions); proptest adds nothing because the sinks are enumerable. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. Nothing in `src/` redacts server text against the key: `grep -rn redact src` finds only the `<redacted>` literals in the two Debug impls (`client.rs:354`, `:510`). `classify` quotes the body for 400/402/403/413/422 and every other status (`client.rs:713-760`, `http::truncate` at `http.rs:466` only cuts length). `Response.extra` is flattened into the recording (`jud/mod.rs:280-292`, `answer.rs:445`). A 401 is safe by construction (`Error::Unauthorized` has no detail field, `client.rs:731`). |
| **Fault angle** | Hostile or debug-mode gateway echoing request headers; OpenAI-style "Incorrect API key provided: sk-..." messages; a reverse proxy error page that reflects the request. |
| **Why it matters** | The recording is meant to be committed (`public_url` exists for exactly that reason, `backend.rs:182-187`), and error text goes to CI logs. This is the one credential path that depends on a third party's behaviour. |
| **Priority** | P1: credential leak into committed files and shared logs; no code defends it. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/client.rs:713-760` (classify), `src/client.rs:790-839` (error_detail), `src/http.rs:466-479` (truncate_to), `src/jud/mod.rs:280-292` (recording_to_yaml keeps extra), `src/answer.rs:445` (`extra`), `src/client.rs:350,507` (Debug impls) |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none for the test. The fix needs the key kept next to the client (a redaction step in `Client::send` / `Reply`), not a test seam. |

**Open Questions:**
- Is redaction of a verbatim key in server text meant to be in scope, or is "do not echo secrets" the server's job? The docs claim only that "no message quotes any part of a key" for the key *validation* errors (`client.rs:877-910` doc). If out of scope, downgrade to a documented limitation and keep only the recording half (drop `extra` or whitelist it).
- A masked echo (`sk-abc***xyz`) is not caught by an exact match; whether partial redaction is wanted is a design question.

---

## Evidence trail
- Read `classify`/`error_detail` (`client.rs:713-839`): all quoting paths end in `http::truncate` (length only). Read `Reply::decode`, `evaluate_with`: `extra` kept, id from body.
- `grep -rn redact src` and `grep -rn 'echo' tests/*.rs`: no test or code echoes the Authorization header back.
- `recording_to_yaml` (`jud/mod.rs:280-292`) serialises the whole `Recording` including `response.extra` (unit test `answer.rs:1392,1425` shows `routing`, `id`, `provider` retained).
- Not verified: exact reqwest behaviour of server-sent `WWW-Authenticate`/headers (ignored by the client); not checked whether OpenRouter or Cloudflare ever echo.

## Decision-gated
Blocked by human decision(s) HD11 (see the decision beads). Until decided, land as a green characterization test or `#[ignore = "HD11"]`; do not commit it red.

title: jud-duplicate-keys-and-parse-totality: Every duplicate key is an error and no input panics the reader
description:
### jud-duplicate-keys-and-parse-totality — Every duplicate key is an error and no input panics the reader

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | (a) `jud::parse` never panics on arbitrary bytes-as-UTF-8-lossy input, including the `unreachable!` at `src/jud/mod.rs:144` (it must stay unreachable because `Envelope::check` has already limited `kind` to the three names; true by construction, but both calls re-parse the text). (b) A duplicate key at every level is `Syntax` (not first/last wins): envelope keys, `metadata`, `labels`, `annotations`, `questions` ids, a Choice's option keys, a Noul's `true`/`false` (bare and quoted spelling together), a case's `expect`, `options`, and keys inside a `state`. Keys that are distinct strings but equal as YAML integers (`0xB` and `11`, `011` and `11`) are a duplicate in unquoted YAML and distinct in quoted/JSON form; the writer must never emit the first form for two distinct strings. |
| **Check** | cargo-fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/jud_parse.rs` calling `jud::parse` (all three kinds) and `Rubric::parse`/`Cases::parse`/`parse_recording`, seeded with `examples/jud/*.jud` and `docs` fenced examples; the only assertion is no panic and no more than a bounded time/memory. Plus proptest in `tests/jud.rs` for (b), duplicating keys by text insertion. No test in `tests/jud*.rs` or `src/jud/` mentions a duplicate key in a `.jud` document (grep for "duplicate" finds only an unrelated option name), although the reading rules state "A duplicate key is an error" (`jud-format.md` Reading rules) and the policy is the saphyr default (`DuplicateKeyPolicy::Error`, `serde-saphyr/src/de/options.rs:510`), not a setting the crate chose. |
| **Expected today** | passes (no panic) and probably passes (duplicates), but nothing in the repo pins either; the default could change on a dependency update. Unknown for duplicate keys inside values buffered through `Value` or `#[serde(flatten)]` (`RawRubric.rest`, `parse_recording::Doc.rest`). |
| **Fault angle** | hostile YAML/JSON documents; dependency upgrade of `serde-saphyr`. |
| **Why it matters** | A last-wins duplicate question id silently drops a question and changes the fingerprint's meaning; a reader that panics on input is a crash in `jud check`. |
| **Priority** | P2: spec MUST with zero tests. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/mod.rs:137-146`, `:311-318`, `src/jud/rubric.rs:264-275`, `src/jud/mod.rs:262-285`, `serde-saphyr-1.3.0/src/de/options.rs:16-34`, `:510` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Does the saphyr duplicate-key policy apply to maps read through `serde_json::Value` and `#[serde(flatten)]` buffers? Insert one duplicate per site.

title: jud-writer-output-is-always-readable: Whatever a server returned, the recording the CLI writes can be read back
description:
### jud-writer-output-is-always-readable — Whatever a server returned, the recording the CLI writes can be read back

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any `Response` that decodes (`serde_json` limit 128 deep) and verifies, `parse_recording(recording_to_yaml(&Recording::new(..)))` returns an equal `Recording`, and `Replay::open` over a directory holding that file succeeds. Includes: top-level `extra` fields nested 1..120 deep, keys and strings from a YAML-hostile alphabet (`<<`, `~`, `null`, `yes`, `0xB`, `11`, `01`, `1_0`, `.inf`, `-`, `?`, `:`, ` `, `#`, `\u{85}`, `\u{2028}`, `\u{FEFF}`, `\0`, `\r`, trailing spaces, 64 KB strings), integers above 2^53 and `u64::MAX`, floats `-0.0`, `5e-324`, `1.7976931348623157e308`, duplicates created only by YAML key equivalence (`0xB` and `11`). Also for `Rubric::to_yaml` and `Cases::to_yaml` with such option keys and states: parse equal, fingerprints equal. |
| **Check** | proptest in `tests/jud.rs` (round trips) and a CLI subprocess test in `tests/jud_record.rs` for the deep-nesting case (wiremock returns a 2xx whose unknown top-level field is 70 deep; run `jud record` twice, assert the second run does not fail with "cannot read the recordings already in"). The CLI test is needed because the poisoning happens across two process runs. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL for nesting, probable; pass for strings and keys (the YAML writer's quoting is deliberate: `serde-saphyr/src/ser/quoting.rs:230-280` quotes `<<`, numeric-looking, edge-whitespace and control strings). The reader's budget is `max_depth: 64` (`serde-saphyr/src/de/budget.rs:283`, default options used at `jud/mod.rs:311-318`) while `Response` decoding allows 128; the recording nests under `spec.response.<field>`, so a server field about 60 levels deep decodes, is written by `render` (`record.rs:588-606`, which verifies against questions but does not re-parse its own YAML) and then cannot be read: `prepare_directory` turns the unreadable `.jud` into a usage failure for every later run over that directory (`record.rs:566-585`), and the library `Replay::open` refuses the whole directory. Unknown for ints above 2^53 until run. |
| **Fault angle** | hostile 2xx (deep or odd extra fields), filesystem content from earlier runs. |
| **Why it matters** | One hostile response can poison a recordings directory (denial of service on `jud record`, `jud eval`, `jud tune`) and the paid-for answer is on disk but unreadable. Round trip is also the claimed conformance condition (`jud-format.md` Schemas and conformance: "writes documents that ... read back unchanged"). |
| **Priority** | P2: probable failure with a clear mechanism, data stays on disk. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/mod.rs:306-318`, `:262-304`, `src/bin/jud/record.rs:566-606`, `src/answer.rs:414-446`, `src/backend.rs` (`Replay::open`), `serde-saphyr-1.3.0/src/de/budget.rs:283` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none; optionally have `render` re-parse its own output before writing (a fix, not a prerequisite). |

**Open Questions:**
- How deep must the server's field be for the document to exceed 64 (count `spec`, `response`, and any flow wrapping)? One run settles the threshold.
- Does the library `Recorder` (`.json`) have the same limit? It writes JSON read by serde_json (128), so probably not.

---

### rubric-reader-refuses-non-wire-scalars — A rubric with a number or boolean where the wire takes text, object, array or null is refused

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | `Rubric::parse` refuses a question whose `instructions`, Noul criterion, Choice option description or Score level is a YAML number or boolean (`instructions: 42`, `criteria: {a: 5}`, `criteria: [1, 2]`, `true: 7`), naming the path, as `Cases::parse` already refuses the same on supplied options; the JSON Schema refuses the same. |
| **Check** | add rows to `refused_documents()` in `tests/jud.rs` (which asserts schema and parser both refuse, `:352-362`): number instructions, boolean instructions, a number Score level, a bool Choice description, a number Noul criterion. A fixed example list is correct here because the claim is concrete and the generator version is `jud-reader-schema-writer-agree`. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. `RawQuestion` reads `instructions` and criteria as `serde_json::Value` (`rubric.rs:288-316`) and `check_question` calls `validate_with` (`rubric.rs:473-475`), which refuses null levels but never number or bool (`question.rs:395-432`); the only scalar check in the reader is for supplied case options (`src/jud/cases.rs:265`). The schema refuses them (`common.schema.json` `description`, `instructions`, score `items` types) and so does the hosted API (422, `tests/contract.rs:857-915` pins the builder gap). Unquoted YAML makes it easy to hit: `high: 10` or `no_match: 0.5` as a description. |
| **Fault angle** | hand-edited YAML (unquoted scalars). |
| **Why it matters** | A rubric the reader accepts but no server accepts: fingerprinted, listed as valid by `jud check`, then `jud record` hits a 422 on every request. A lenient server (Laya/Ollama shims) may instead accept and echo a number level, so the same file works on one server and not another. |
| **Priority** | P2: confirmed by reading, same class as the 0.5.1 fix for case options. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/rubric.rs:288-316`, `:473-475`, `src/question.rs:395-432`, `src/jud/cases.rs:262-272`, `schemas/jud/common.schema.json` (`instructions`, `description`, score `items`) |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Should the refusal live in `validate_with` (so the builder refuses it too, closing the documented builder gap) or only in the reader? The former changes the library API.

---

Rubric::parse accepted numeric, boolean and array `instructions` (5, true, 1.5, [1]); 5 round-trips as `instructions: 5`. Only null is refused.

### rubric-version-number-is-read-as-its-text — `metadata.version: 1.10` is written back as `1.10`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any `metadata.version` scalar the spec allows (string, or a number "read as its text", `jud-format.md` metadata table), `Rubric::parse` followed by `to_yaml` followed by `parse` yields the same `version` string, and that string is the source spelling: `1.10`, `2.0`, `010`, `1e3`, `0x10` keep their spelling. A non-string, non-number `version` (`true`, `[1]`, `{a: 1}`) is refused. |
| **Check** | unit test in `src/jud/rubric.rs` tests (next to the existing `version: 3` at `:999`, `:1041`): parse `version: 1.10`, assert `rubric.version == Some("1.10")`. Rows for `2.0`, `010`, `1e3`, `0x10`, `1_000`, `.5`. Then a round-trip assertion through `to_yaml`. Add the three refusal rows to the differential. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. `RawRubric.metadata.version` is an `Option<Value>` (`jud/mod.rs:202-212`); a YAML number reaches `Value::Number` and is then rendered with `other.to_string()` (`rubric.rs:594-597`), which prints the parsed number, not the source text (`1.10` becomes `1.1`, `1e3` becomes `1000.0`, `010` becomes `10`, `0x10` becomes `16`). `bool`, array and object are also rendered through the same arm instead of being refused. `to_yaml` then writes the normalised string (`rubric.rs:624`), so `jud tune --out` and `jud split` rewrite a rubric whose version changed. The version is not in any fingerprint (`jud-format.md`), so nothing flags it. |
| **Fault angle** | hand-written version numbers; rewrite by `tune`/`split`. |
| **Why it matters** | Silent edit of a user field on every rewrite; a "2.10" edition turning into "2.1" collides with a different edition. Contradicts the spec sentence "a number is read as its text". |
| **Priority** | P2: confirmed by reading `rubric.rs:594-597`, silent data change, small blast radius. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/rubric.rs:594-597`, `:624`, `src/jud/mod.rs:202-212`, `docs/reference/jud-format.md` (metadata table) |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Does serde-saphyr hand a plain-scalar number to `Value::deserialize` as `Number` rather than as a string? The test settles it; if it hands strings the entry is a pass and `1e3` still needs a look.

description:
### jud-apiversion-is-refused-by-name-before-anything-else — A document of another version is `Version`, whatever follows

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any text whose top-level `apiVersion` is a scalar other than the string `jud/v1.3` (including `jud/v1.3 `, `jud/V1.3`, `"jud/v1.3\n"`, `1.3`, `!!str jud/v9`, a mapping, a long string), `jud::parse`, `Rubric::parse`, `Cases::parse` and `parse_recording` return `Error::Version` (or `Missing` when absent), even when the rest of the document uses things the v1.3 reader refuses: a custom tag, a merge key `<<`, a duplicate key in an unrelated mapping, nesting past 64, an unknown top-level key, an unknown `kind`. A document whose apiVersion is right and kind wrong is `Kind` or `OtherKind`. |
| **Check** | proptest in `tests/jud.rs`. Generator: a valid document skeleton with the envelope key positions shuffled, `apiVersion` drawn from the hostile list, and a tail drawn from {valid, tagged scalar, `<<: *a`, duplicate key, 70-deep flow sequence, 300 KB scalar, unclosed bracket after the envelope}. Assert the error variant. The jud spec says "MUST be refused by name, before anything else in the document is read" (`docs/reference/jud-format.md` section The apiVersion), and decision 0018 makes it the compatibility mechanism. Existing test `the_envelope_is_checked_first` (`mod.rs:430-465`) uses five fixed values with a minimal body. |
| **Expected today** | unknown, likely EXPECTED TO FAIL for the hostile tails. `parse` and every kind's `parse` first deserialize `Envelope` with the same strict saphyr options over the whole stream (`mod.rs:137-139`, `:311-318`); the options reject tags and merge keys and the budget (depth 64) are enforced at the event layer, so an unrelated `!tag` or a 70-deep structure after the envelope would surface as `Error::Syntax` rather than `Version`. Whether duplicate keys in skipped values trip the policy depends on saphyr's skip path. One test settles it. A future `jud/v1.4` document that adds a tag or an anchor construct would then be reported as a syntax error instead of "not a version this crate reads". |
| **Fault angle** | hostile or future-version documents; YAML parser limits (depth 64, 250k nodes, tags, merge keys). |
| **Why it matters** | The whole forward-compatibility story is "refused by name" (`CLAUDE.md`, decision 0018). A refusal that names the wrong cause sends the user to debug YAML instead of upgrading. |
| **Priority** | P2: spec MUST, likely violated for exactly the future-format case it exists for. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/jud/mod.rs:137-146`, `:150-182`, `:311-318`, `tests/jud.rs:367-395`, `docs/reference/jud-format.md` section The apiVersion |
| **Instrumentation needed** | possibly a permissive first-pass envelope reader (options without `reject_unsupported_tags`, a huge depth budget) if the test fails; not needed to write the test. |

**Open Questions:**
- Does saphyr surface a tag or depth error while skipping unknown fields of a struct with no `deny_unknown_fields`? A one-line `parse` call settles it.

title: duplicate-option-keys-are-refused: Two options with one key are an error, not a silent merge
description:
### duplicate-option-keys-are-refused — Two options with one key are an error, not a silent merge

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | `Questions::choice::<O>` returns `InvalidQuestion` when two variants of `O` share `key()`; `Questions::dynamic_choice` returns `InvalidQuestion` when two `(key, description)` pairs share a key. Corollary: the number of options on the wire equals the number of variants/pairs given. |
| **Check** | unit tests in `src/question.rs`. (1) `options! { A = "x" => .., B = "x" => .., C = "y" => .. }`, `choice::<E>` then assert `Err`; (2) `dynamic_choice` with `[("x", Some("1")), ("x", Some("2")), ("y", None)]`, assert `Err`. A unit test is enough; the defect needs one construction. Add a `Options::ALL` uniqueness assertion helper for caller test suites if wanted. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. Both builders `collect()` into an `IndexMap<String, Value>` (`question.rs:263-277`, `:288-298`): a repeated key overwrites the earlier value (keeping the first position), so the question silently has fewer options than the caller gave. For the typed form the second variant becomes unreachable: `O::from_key` returns the first match (`question.rs:118-121` area, `Options::from_key`), so a model answering `"x"` is always read as variant `A`. With only two variants sharing one key the question has one option and is refused by the minimum-2 rule, with a message that does not name the duplicate. |
| **Fault angle** | none (programming error made easy by the macro). |
| **Why it matters** | Silent wrong answer: caller code branches on variant `B` that can never be returned. Ids already refuse duplicates (`DuplicateQuestionId`, `question.rs:343-360`), so options are the inconsistent case. |
| **Priority** | P2: silent wrong answer, but needs a copy-paste mistake in an enum. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/question.rs:263-277`, `:288-298`, `:118-121`, `:343-360` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Should the `options!` macro also reject duplicates at compile time? A `const` assertion is possible but the runtime refusal is the minimum.

title: wire-order-is-insertion-order: Questions and options reach the wire in insertion order
description:
### wire-order-is-insertion-order — Questions and options reach the wire in insertion order

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For any permutation of question ids and of a Choice's option keys, the bytes `Client` sends list the questions, and each Choice's options, in insertion order (byte offset of `"id"` strictly increasing in insertion order), for `evaluate`, `evaluate_with` with `CallOptions::extra`, and through the `SystemOne` trait. Independent of whether `serde_json` has `preserve_order` unified in by another crate. |
| **Check** | proptest wrapping a wiremock server in `tests/client.rs`: generate 2..8 questions with ids drawn from a shuffled non-alphabetical pool and Choices with 2..12 non-alphabetical keys; capture `received_requests()[0].body` bytes and compare the order of `"<id>":{` occurrences and option keys with the insertion order. Raw bytes, not `serde_json::from_slice` plus `==`: `tests/client.rs:1148` compares the body to `serde_json::to_vec(&request)` (same serializer) and `tests/contract.rs:688` compares parsed `Value`s, both blind to order. Only the CLI path is witnessed by position today (`tests/jud_loop.rs:44-70`, `internals.md:156`). |
| **Expected today** | passes. `Questions` serialises as a transparent `IndexMap` (`question.rs:208-211`) and the body is streamed through `#[serde(flatten)]` structs, no `Value` in between (`client.rs:328-333`, `:579`). The risk is future: `serde_json = "1"` has no `preserve_order` (`Cargo.toml:82`); `question.rs:520-560` (`null_instructions_are_sent_as_null`) asserts alphabetical output of `to_value`, which would fail loudly if a dependency enabled the feature. Also note, as a characterization: structured instruction/criteria objects (`Value::Object`) are always sent key-sorted (documented, `jud-format.md` Reading rules: "this crate sends them sorted"). |
| **Fault angle** | none beyond feature unification; the failure would be silent (model sees a different order, recordings and fingerprints unchanged). |
| **Why it matters** | `CLAUDE.md` calls the order "the order the model sees"; the OpenHuman caller sorts on its own side so does not exercise it, but any caller that relies on option order for priming would see a silent change. |
| **Priority** | P2: core claim with no library-path witness. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/question.rs:208-211`, `src/client.rs:328-333`, `:579-583`, `Cargo.toml:82`, `tests/client.rs:1148`, `tests/contract.rs:688`, `tests/jud_loop.rs:44-70` |

title: verify-score-scale-is-exact: A Score verifies iff legend, probability keys and value are on the scale sent
description:
### verify-score-scale-is-exact — A Score verifies iff legend, probability keys and value are on the scale sent

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For a Score question with levels `L` (2..=10), `verify` is `Ok` iff all hold: the legend has exactly `n` entries keyed `"0".."n-1"` in canonical decimal; each entry equals the level sent (string level: exact string, never parsed; structured level: equal `Value`, or a string that parses to an equal `Value`); every probability key is a canonical decimal below `n`; and `-1e-9 <= score <= (n-1) + 1e-9` (NaN and infinities excluded). |
| **Check** | proptest in `src/answer.rs` tests with an independent oracle written from the doc (`answer.rs:44-52` of the module docs), not from `score_fits`. Generator: levels of string / object / array; echoes as value, as compact text, as pretty text, as text with different key order, as string level that looks like JSON (`"{\"a\":1}"` sent as a string must not match a structured echo); numbers that print differently (`1` vs `1.0`, `1e0`); keys `"00"`, `"+1"`, `"1 "`, `"１"`, `"18446744073709551616"`; scores at `±1e-9`, `±2e-9`, `n-1+1e-9`, `-0.0`, `f64::MAX`, `NaN`, `±inf`. Boundary equality on `1e-9` is where an off-by-one in `<`/`<=` or a change of epsilon would hide; examples cover only `3+1e-10` and `-1e-10` (`answer.rs:1867-1890`). |
| **Expected today** | passes for `verify`. One doc-level discrepancy surfaces: `Score::value` is documented as `0.0 ..= levels.len() - 1` (`answer.rs:734`), but `verify` admits `-1e-9` and `top + 1e-9`, so a verified Score can carry a value outside its documented range by a hair (harmless to `nearest_index`, which clamps, `answer.rs:751-753`, but a caller doing `levels[value as usize]`-style code on the raw field would see `-1e-9 as usize == 0` and `top+1e-9` as `top` only after truncation). Treat as a doc fix or a clamp, P3. |
| **Fault angle** | hostile 2xx; the two known server echo behaviours (hosted echoes the value, Laya echoes Python-rendered text, `docs/project/verification/laya-typed-decisions.md:150`). |
| **Why it matters** | A Score is the primitive whose scale a caller computes with (thresholds on `value`); an unverified legend lets a server answer a different rubric than the one sent. |
| **Priority** | P2: the boundary and echo-form space is large and the 0.4.x history shows the echo form moved once (`4852f46`). |
| **Code anchors** | `src/answer.rs:83`, `:541-580`, `:584-588`, `:592-606`, `:751-753` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Is `Score::value` meant to be clamped to the scale after verify? Settles by owner decision.

title: response-decode-is-total-and-never-widens: Hostile JSON decodes to an error or to an in-range value, never panics
description:
### response-decode-is-total-and-never-widens — Hostile JSON decodes to an error or to an in-range value, never panics

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For arbitrary bytes (valid UTF-8 or not) fed to `serde_json::from_str::<Response>`: no panic, no stack overflow, no allocation beyond input size times a small constant; `Ok(r)` implies every `Probability` and `Confidence` in `r` is in `[0,1]`, `usage` counts are `u64`, and `r.request_id` is `None` or a string; `Err` Display is at most 200 bytes regardless of input (existing test pins one case, `answer.rs:1195-1198`). Documented decode rules hold as a table: `null`/absent `usage` and counts are zero, string/negative/fractional counts are `Decode`, missing `confidence` is `Decode`, unknown top-level fields land in `extra`, fields inside an answer are ignored, duplicate keys inside an answer are last-wins, `1e999`/`-1e999` anywhere (even in an unknown top-level field) is `Decode`, nesting past serde_json's 128 limit is `Decode`. |
| **Check** | Two mechanisms. (1) proptest in `src/answer.rs` tests: structure-aware generator of JSON text (valid skeleton, then splice in `null`, huge exponents, 129-deep arrays, duplicated keys, wrong types, lone surrogate escapes `"\ud800"`) asserting the invariants above; (2) a cargo-fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/response_decode.rs` over raw bytes through `String::from_utf8_lossy` (what `http.rs:417` does), same assertions. Proptest for the table, fuzz for the unstructured space. |
| **Expected today** | passes for no-panic and in-range. Two divergences to pin as characterization tests (not defects): (a) a duplicate top-level `model`/`answers`/`usage` key is probably a `Decode` error ("duplicate field", serde derive with `flatten`, `answer.rs:414-446`) while a duplicate inside an answer is last-wins (`answer.rs:307-313`, test `answer.rs:1202`); the docs only state the latter. (b) `usage.input_tokens: 12.0` is a `Decode` of the whole response (documented as fractional, `answer.rs:337-351` area), which for a billed call loses the answer for a float spelling; a Python-based server that computes tokens as float would trigger it. Unknown until run: whether (a) errors. |
| **Fault angle** | server sends odd JSON: null, wrong types, huge numbers, duplicate keys, unknown fields, deep nesting. |
| **Why it matters** | This is the trust boundary for every backend; a panic here is a crash of the caller after a billed call. |
| **Priority** | P2: no known defect, but the surface is the widest in the crate and has no generator-based test. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/answer.rs:313-335`, `:340-371`, `:414-446`, `:112-115` (Probability), `src/http.rs:405-419`, `src/client.rs:591` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none (fuzz target is new tooling; proptest dev-dependency) |

**Open Questions:**
- Does a duplicate top-level key error or last-win under `#[serde(flatten)]`? One `from_str` call settles it.

description:
### verify-choice-offered-set-is-exact — A Choice verifies iff the choice and every distribution key were offered

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | For a Choice question with criteria set `C` and any Choice answer `(choice, probabilities)`: `verify` is `Ok` iff `choice ∈ C` and every key of `probabilities` is in `C`, by exact `str` equality (no trimming, case folding, Unicode normalisation, prefix match). An unknown-kind answer under an asked id, a kind with different case (`"Choice"`), or a non-string `type` is never `Ok`. Answers for unasked ids never influence the result. |
| **Check** | proptest in `src/answer.rs` tests (oracle is a one-line set comparison, so the property is `verify.is_ok() == oracle`). Generator for option keys: ASCII, whitespace-padded variants, NFC/NFD pairs (`"é"` vs `"e\u{301}"`), case variants, `\u{FFFD}`, empty string, 255 keys, keys of 4 KiB. Mutations of the answer: add or remove a distribution key, swap `choice`, rename `type` to `"Choice"`/`"choice "`/`5`/`null`. For the `type` cases go through `serde_json::from_value::<Response>` so the decoder is in the loop. Differential against an oracle rather than example tests because the existing ones (`answer.rs:1648-1700`) pin two shapes. |
| **Expected today** | passes. `verify_answer` chains `choice` with `probabilities.keys()` and `criteria.contains_key` (`answer.rs:497-512`); `Answer::deserialize` keeps unknown strings as `Unknown` and refuses non-string `type` (`answer.rs:313-335`); a kind mismatch is `AnswerTypeMismatch` (`:524-529`). An offered option missing from the distribution is deliberately accepted (`answer.rs:60-62`), so the oracle must not require full coverage. |
| **Fault angle** | hostile 2xx: off-list option, near-miss option strings from a lenient or buggy server. |
| **Why it matters** | `CLAUDE.md`: "An off-list option is an error, never a default". It is the one guard between a model's free text and a caller's branch. |
| **Priority** | P2: central claim, currently only example-tested. |

description:
### choice-handle-is-checked-against-offered-options — A `Choice<O>` handle cannot disagree with the options sent

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | `Questions::handle::<Choice<O>>(id)` returns `Some` only when every key of the question's `criteria` is a key of `O::ALL`; equivalently, if `verify` accepts a Choice answer then `get` of any handle the questions hand out does not return `UnknownOption`. |
| **Check** | Unit test in `src/question.rs` tests. Build `q.dynamic_choice("c", .., [("billing",..),("sales",..)])`, take `q.handle::<Choice<Dept>>("c")` (where `Dept` has no `sales`), build a response whose choice is `"sales"` (offered, so `verify` accepts it), then `get(&handle)`. Assert either `handle(..)` is `None` or `get` is `Ok`. Second case: `choice::<A>` then `handle::<Choice<B>>` for two enums with different keys. A unit test is enough: the failure needs one specific construction, no generator. |
| **Expected today** | EXPECTED TO FAIL. `Questions::handle` compares only `question.kind() == A::KIND` (`question.rs:329-335`), `A::KIND` is `"choice"` for every `Choice<O>` (`answer.rs:682`), and `Choice<O>::from_answer` returns `UnknownOption` for a key outside `O::ALL` (`answer.rs:688-700`). `verify` accepts the same key because it checks only the question's criteria (`answer.rs:497-512`). So `verify` Ok, `get` Err, against the doc at `answer.rs:36-38`. The fix is to refuse the handle (or to check in `get`). |
| **Fault angle** | none (API misuse reachable through a public method; also a rubric lowered from a `.jud` file read through a handle of a hand-written enum). |
| **Why it matters** | The documented "get cannot fail after verify" has a hole at exactly the place a rubric-driven caller (dynamic options, typed enum) is most likely to step in. The error is loud (`UnknownOption`), not silent, so impact is a spurious failure after a billed call. |
| **Priority** | P2: confirmed by reading, loud failure, small fix. |
| **Code anchors** | `src/question.rs:329-335`, `src/answer.rs:681-700`, `src/answer.rs:497-512`, `src/answer.rs:36-38` |
| **Instrumentation needed** | none |

**Open Questions:**
- Is the intended fix in `handle` (needs `O::ALL` at handle time, so `FromAnswer` needs a hook) or in `get`? Settles only by a design choice.

| **Property** | With one `Client` (and one `Fake`, `Replay`, `Recorder<Fake>` over distinct states) shared by N = 32 concurrent tasks on a multi-thread runtime, each call gets the response built for its own request (own question ids, own `CallOptions` headers and extras), each call's attempt count is its own (a task whose first attempt gets 503 reports `attempts = 2`, the others 1), `Fake::calls()` has exactly N entries, and `Client`, `Replay`, `Fake`, `Recorder<Fake>`, `Response`, `Error`, `Completed`, `Exhausted` are `Send + Sync` and the futures of `evaluate_with` and `send_with_retries(.., Send closure)` are `Send`. |
| **Check** | (1) A compile-time test (`tests/send_sync.rs`): `fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}` and `fn assert_send<F: Send>(_: &F) {}` for the types above and for `tokio::spawn(client.evaluate_with(..))` (needs `Client` by clone and an owned request). The only guarantee today is the `SystemOne: Send + Sync` bound (`backend.rs:38`) on four impls. (2) A runtime test in `tests/client.rs` with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]` and a custom `wiremock::Respond` that reads the request body, takes the question ids and the per-call header, and answers with exactly those ids; failure injection is a stateful responder returning 503 to the first request of every even-numbered state. Cross-talk surfaces as `MissingAnswer`/mismatched header. wiremock `Respond` fits: the property is about request/response pairing. |

| **Check** | `tests/client.rs` (observer-free, wiremock/raw server): `tokio::time::timeout(100 ms, client.system_one(..))` against (a) a mock with `set_delay(1 s)`, (b) a raw server that sends headers then stalls, (c) a 503 mock with 500 ms backoff, (d) a 429 with `Retry-After: 2`. After the elapsed, sleep 3x the wait and assert `received_requests().len()` unchanged, then run a good call on the same client. In an own binary also assert the global observer count is unchanged by the drop. `Recorder<Client>`: drop inside `inner.answer` leaves no file in the directory (nothing is written, `backend.rs:371,385`). wiremock for (a),(c),(d); raw server for (b). |

(2) `tests/jud_cli.rs` subprocess with `config_home()` holding `timeout_secs: 0` and a wiremock server: assert exit code and that stderr either contains `timeout_secs` or the server got one request. | **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | Over any call, the number of `on_failed_attempt` reports from the retry loop equals the number of attempts that failed (non-2xx status, transport failure, or too-large body), one report per attempt; `on_usage` is called exactly once for each 2xx that decodes (fit or unfit) and never for decode failures, transport failures or error statuses. |
| **Check** | New own-binary `tests/observer_counts.rs` with a recording `Observer` installed by `set_global` and a raw scripted server: (a) 503 then 503 then 200: expect reports `["503","503"]`, usage 1; (b) 503 with body cut short: one report expected; (c) 503 with body over the cap: one report expected; (d) 200 undecodable: `decode` once, usage 0; (e) `Replay`/`Fake` call: nothing. | **Type** | Safety |
| **Property** | Under `RetryPolicy::conservative()` (statuses {408,429}, `TransportRetry::BeforeSend`), for every server script, a request the server fully read and answered or abandoned in any way other than a complete 408/429 response is never followed by another request of the same call; a second request occurs only after a refused/failed connect or a complete 408/429. |

Assert: per script, number of connections that read a complete request (server-side flag) is `<= 1 + number of leading complete-408/429 answers`. Also `Never` and `BeforeSend` on the same alphabet.
