# SUT discovery E: external dependencies (focus 9) and product context (focus 10)

Commit 56acead. Read-only pass over `src/`, `tests/live.rs`, `docs/project/verification/*.md`, `docs/project/research/*.md`, `docs/guides/*`. Nothing was run. Everything from the verification pages is a lead: those pages record what a person observed on a date, not what a server does today. Where I read the code myself I say so and give the line.

## 0. Framing

The crate talks to one wire (`POST /v1/systemone`, `GET /v1/models`) on servers it does not control. It has no server of its own. Its external surface is:

1. the HTTP peer (hosted, local or gateway),
2. the process environment (`TYPESAFE_*`, `JUD_*`, proxy variables, `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`),
3. the filesystem (config file, rubric and cases, recording directories),
4. the process-global observer and `fastrand`.

Focus 9 yields a lot because the departures are catalogued. The crate's defence is the same everywhere: tolerant decoding, strict `Response::verify`, and a classified `Error`. It does not model per-server limits. Option caps and level caps are constants (255 and 10, `docs/project/research/compatible-servers-and-models.md`, "Expose backend limits as data").

## 1. Server-by-server departures and how the code absorbs them

"Verified" means a page under `docs/project/verification/` records a run. "Doc" means taken from vendor documentation or release notes, never run against this crate.

| Server | Departs from hosted API in | Status of evidence | How `src/` absorbs it (or does not) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hosted TypeSafe** `https://api.typesafe.ai` (default, `DEFAULT_BASE_URL`) | The reference. 255 options, 2..10 levels (400 beyond). Three 400 body shapes (string `detail`; object `{error_type, message}`; `{"detail":{"error_type":"max_tokens_exceeded"}}` with no message). Missing key is 403, wrong key 401. Extra top-level field is 400 `Invalid request.` naming nothing. Extra field inside a question is silently ignored. Not deterministic: the same request varies by 0.01 to 0.19 in top probability, confidence by up to 0.28 on ambiguous inputs. `jev-latest` is an alias that resolves to `jev-1.13.0`. | Verified 2026-10-03 | `classify` (`src/client.rs:713-756`) maps 400/413/422 to `InvalidRequest` (with `kind` from `error_detail`), 401, 403, 429, 529, other to `Http`. `Response::model` carries the resolved version. `Error::is_request_too_large` names the `max_tokens_exceeded` case. The builder refuses 0 or 1 option, duplicate ids, a null level and an empty key before the wire. Nondeterminism is not absorbed at all: a recording is one draw. |
| **Laya** `laya-serve` 0.3.24 to 0.3.26, local | No `GET /v1/models` (404). `model` field is `laya-rl-agent` for every checkpoint; the checkpoint is in top-level `routing`. The request `model` routes by name; an unknown name is routed, not refused. `confidence` is one minus normalised entropy (not TypeSafe's spread). No request-id header. Limits answered 413: more than 64 questions, 50,000 chars of state, 2 MiB body, 100 options, 32 levels, 512 options in all. Empty question id is 422. Structured Score level echoed as JSON text since 0.3.22. Answers 503 with `Retry-After: 1` past 16 concurrent. Seconds per request on CPU; 78 s on first load of an unloaded checkpoint. Extra answer-level fields (`answer_confidence`, `action`, `abstention`) exist. | Verified 2026-10-03 (0.3.24, CPU stand-in machine) | `Response::extra` keeps `routing`. Answer-level extras are dropped by serde (not modelled). `Response::verify` compares a structured level by its parsed value (text echo allowed). 413 is `InvalidRequest`, not retried. 503 is retried under the default policy and honours `Retry-After`. Default timeout is 10 s in the library, 30 s in `jud` (`config.rs:DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS`); a cold load exceeds either, and a timeout is retried (`TransportRetry::Any`) up to twice, so one cold start can cost three attempts. `confidence` semantics are not absorbed: the typed `Confidence` accepts any value in `[0,1]`. |
| **Ollama** 0.35+ (`/v1/systemone`), local | 2..26 options and levels per question (400), 1..64 questions per request (400). Object Score level refused (400). `GET /v1/models` is OpenAI-shaped. Missing model is 404 `model "x" not found`. Bearer ignored. No request id. `confidence` is the model's own formula. A loader killed by the OOM killer appears as a dropped connection. | Doc page `configure-a-backend.md` says "Observed 2026-10-07 against Ollama 0.40.0 with `tev1:0.8b`", but `compatible-servers-and-models.md` (2026-10-06) still says "not yet observed" and there is no verification page. Treat as partly observed, no record in `verification/`. | Builder cap is 255, so 27..255 options go to the wire and come back `InvalidRequest` (not retried): the crate absorbs this only as an error. `list_models` fails with `Error::Decode` (and bumps the `decode` failed-attempt counter). A dropped connection is `Transport{attempts:3}`, retried three times by default. `jud` refuses to build without a key even though Ollama ignores it. |
| **autojev-serve** (pplx-decider-v1.1-27b server) | 422 `HTTPValidationError` for 256 options, 11 levels, 1 level, unknown extra field. Empty question id answered under key `""`. No token budget before the model. Noul answer carries no `confidence` (allowed by the schema; the crate has no Noul confidence). `output_tokens` always 0. Answers to `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, `jev-1.13.0` as aliases. 401 on wrong bearer when `AUTOJEV_API_KEY` set. | Verified 2026-10-09 with a stand-in for the network; real weights not run | 422 is `InvalidRequest`. Lenient `Usage` reads missing counts as 0 (`src/answer.rs:387-405`). Because the server answers to Jev aliases, a recording says `model: jev-...` while a different server answered (docs say to name the model `autojev-qwen3.8-27b` instead). Confidence of Choice and Score under the real model unobserved. |
| **OpenRouter System One** `https://openrouter.ai/api` | Body plus `id` (`gen-dec-...`), `provider`, `usage.cost` (USD). No `x-typesafe-request-id`. 402 when credit runs out. `jev-latest` routes as `~typesafe/jev-latest`; response `model` is a dated id (`typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917`). `GET /api/v1/models` is the OpenRouter catalogue. Same body also at `/api/alpha/decisions`. | Doc only; client run against a stand-in built from the documented shapes 2026-10-09; `mise run live:openrouter` never run | Base-URL path prefix kept: `build` appends `/` so `Url::join` does not drop the `api` segment (`src/client.rs:453-459`; CHANGELOG records that it used to). `Usage::cost` read leniently (`number_or_none`). `request_id` falls back to the body `id` only when the header is absent, after the `usable_request_id` checks (`client.rs:595-605`). 402 is `Error::PaymentRequired`, not retried (`client.rs:736`). `list_models` fails to decode. The `Profile::OpenRouter` in `tests/live.rs:97-102` pins nothing but the model-list behaviour. |
| **Cloudflare Clef** (Workers AI), via `tools/systemone/serve.py cloudflare` | Different URL per model, no `/v1/systemone`, result wrapped in `{"result","success","errors"}`, 64 questions per request. | Doc plus the shim; `live:clef` not run | The crate cannot reach it with a base URL alone; it depends entirely on the Python shim (outside `src/`) to map the path, unwrap the envelope and forward `Retry-After` and `cf-ray`. The Cloudflare token comes from the shim's environment, not the bearer. |
| **Google Cloud** (study only) | Cloud Run (A) and a gateway (D) are plain base URLs. Vertex `rawPredict` (B, C) has a one-URL-per-endpoint path with `:rawPredict`, OAuth/ID tokens that expire in about an hour, Google's own error body shape. | Research note only (2026-10-06) | Path B is not reachable: `Client::url("v1/systemone")` always joins onto the base. The bearer is fixed at `build` (`client.rs:465-472`), so a token that expires mid-process produces 401 and a `Client` rebuild is the caller's job. Per-call `authorization` header is refused as `ReservedHeader`. |
| Unverified others (Decider, OpenDecider 26 options, Perplexity hosted, Fastino, meraGPT) | Option caps differ (26 for OpenDecider), confidence semantics differ. | Doc | Same as Ollama: caps surface only as 400s. |

### 1.1 Cross-server behaviours to hold the crate to

- **Required `confidence`.** `Choice` and `Score` answers require `confidence`; a missing one is `Error::Decode` for the whole response (`src/answer.rs:263-275`, test at `answer.rs:1148`). Usage is billed and the observer's `on_usage` is not called for a decode failure: it is called only after a successful decode (`client.rs:619`). Only the failed-attempt counter sees it. A server that omits it on a Choice (never observed) would cost money and report none.
- **Retry of billed calls.** Default `RetryPolicy` retries every 5xx and every transport failure, including a body cut mid-read (`http.rs:345-353`). The docs themselves say the API reference does not say whether a 5xx or timeout was charged (`http.rs:171-177`). `RetryPolicy::conservative()` exists but is not the default, and `jud` uses the default.
- **Redirects off** (`client.rs:478`). A gateway or captive portal that answers 301/302 becomes `Error::Http{status:3xx}` with the body truncated. The `Authorization` header is never forwarded to a redirect target (good).
- **No `no_proxy()`** in the builder (`client.rs:474-479`), so `reqwest` reads `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` from the environment. A local server (Ollama, Laya at 127.0.0.1) is routed through a configured proxy unless `NO_PROXY` covers it. This sandbox itself has such a proxy. I did not check whether `reqwest` 0.13 bypasses loopback automatically; settle with a wiremock test under `HTTP_PROXY` set.
- **TLS roots** come from the platform verifier (`rustls-platform-verifier`, `Cargo.lock:1559`). The scratch container image ships `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` (`Dockerfile`, `docs/reference/container-image.md:20`). A host with no roots is a `Transport` error with `attempts: 0` at build time or a retried handshake failure at call time.
- **Process-global observer.** `observer::set_global` is a `OnceLock`, first call wins (`src/observer.rs`). Failed attempts always go to the global one, usage to the client's own when set. In a process with two clients and two observers, failed attempts of both land on one observer, labelled only `service` (`"typesafe"`), not by base URL.
- **`fastrand`** supplies jitter (`http.rs:203`), unseeded and process-global. It only subtracts from a delay (max 25% by default), so it cannot lengthen a wait; it makes timing tests non-deterministic except via `delay_with`.
- **Clock.** `Retry-After` dates are measured against the response `Date` header, falling back to local time (`http.rs:450-454`). Values above `retry_after_max` (30 s) are replaced by the backoff, silently.
- **Response size.** 8 MiB body cap, checked on `Content-Length` and while streaming (`http.rs:404-419`).
- **Non-UTF-8 bodies** are repaired lossily and then fail JSON decode (or not) (`http.rs:417`).

### 1.2 What `tests/live.rs` pins per server (the `Profile` enum)

- Profiles: `Typesafe`, `Laya`, `Autojev`, `OpenRouter`, `Generic` (`tests/live.rs:89-106`).
- Limits (`limit_status`, line 180): hosted 400 for 256 options and 11 levels; Laya 413 for 256 options, 200 for 11 levels, 1 option, 1 level; autojev 422 for 256 options, 11 levels and 1 level, 200 for 1 option; OpenRouter and Generic unpinned.
- Empty id (`empty_id_status`): hosted 400, Laya 422, autojev 200, others unpinned.
- Over budget (`over_budget_status`): hosted 400, Laya 413, others unpinned.
- Schema conformance is asserted only for hosted and autojev (`holds_to_the_schema`); Laya's bodies are only printed.
- A billed host (`api.typesafe.ai`, `openrouter.ai`) with no `JUDGMENT_LIVE_PROFILE` panics instead of falling to `generic` (`from_env`, line 137-166). A billed server reached by another hostname (a gateway, a Cloud Run proxy) falls to `generic` silently.
- No profile for Ollama, Clef or Perplexity: `live:ollama` and `live:pplx` run as `Generic`/`Autojev`, so Ollama's 26-option cap is never asserted by a test, only documented.

### 1.3 Filesystem and environment as dependencies of `jud`

- Config file: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jud/config.yaml` else `$HOME/.config/jud/config.yaml` else relative `.config/jud/config.yaml` when neither variable is set (`config.rs:path`). With `HOME` unset the config is looked up relative to the current directory: a file in a checked-out repository would then be read. Open question whether any container image sets `HOME` (the image sets `/home/jud`).
- Precedence: base URL and key are env then file; **the model has no environment variable** and comes only from the file or the default `jev-latest` (`config.rs:resolve`). A blank or whitespace `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` is filtered out (`env_var`) and falls to the file or the hosted default, so a blank variable sends paid calls to the hosted API.
- Misspelt variables with a `TYPESAFE_` or `JUD_` prefix are named on stderr before a call (`warn_ignored_environment`), but only for `Backend::open` against a server; a variable with another prefix (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `JUDGMENT_BASE_URL`) is not noticed.
- Reads are unbounded `read_to_string` of stdin, rubric, cases and recordings (`run.rs:read_state`, `tools.rs:read_document`, `backend.rs:read`). Hostile or huge input is a memory question; YAML bounds depend on `serde-saphyr` (not read).
- Recording writes are atomic by temp file plus rename with `sync_all` on the file, not on the directory (`record.rs:620-632`). A crash after rename can still lose the entry on some filesystems. Two `jud record` processes on one directory both write distinct temp names (pid in the name) and can both pay for the same case (each reads `known` once at start, `record.rs:360`).

## 2. Product context: what a user sees and which workflows matter

Workflows, in rough order of how much they are advertised (`main.rs` help, `docs/guides/run-in-ci.md`, `plugins/jud/README.md`):

1. **`jud RUBRIC < state.json`**: one JSON verdict per question on stdout, status 0, 1, or 2. Spends one call. Does not announce the server (`announce` is called only from `record` and `batch::answer_all`).
2. **`jud record RUBRIC CASES --out DIR`**: pay once. A request already recorded under the same fingerprint is "kept" and not asked again (`record.rs:394-405`). Resume after an interruption is by design.
3. **`jud eval ... --replay DIR --min-accuracy X`**: the CI gate, exit 3 on a miss, exit 1 on a missing recording.
4. **`jud tune`**: proposes gate bars from recordings (best F1 for a Noul; the lowest confidence bar that keeps `--target-accuracy` 0.95 over at least `--min-covered` 3 cases for Choice/Score).
5. **Rust API**: `Client`, typed handles, `Fake`, `Recorder`, `Replay` behind `&dyn SystemOne`.
6. **Claude Code plugin** (`plugins/jud/`): `/jud:record` plans with `--dry-run` and states the cost before spending; commands run `jud` only through a script and one command per Bash call.

An application like OpenHuman uses (5) with hand-set thresholds and no calibration data. For it the wire's alphabetised options, nondeterminism and per-server `confidence` meaning are the live risks (see section 4).

## 3. Ranked user-visible failure modes

Ranked by (user harm x likelihood that nobody notices). Each is a lead to confirm with a named check, not an established defect unless I say I read the line.

1. **A replay or `record` run that mixes servers and models without saying so.** Read in code: `Replay::answer` ignores its `model` argument (`src/backend.rs:512-520`, `_model`), the fingerprint excludes the model (`eval/canonical.rs:36-38`), and `jud record`'s `held` asks `Replay` with the backend's model, which is ignored (`record.rs:432-448`). So `jud record` into a directory recorded under another server prints `kept <case>` for every case and spends nothing, then `jud eval --replay` grades the old server's answers while the operator believes they measured the new one. `jud tune` refuses mixed `Response::model` values (`tune.rs:650-683`) but `eval` and `record` do not, and Laya answers `model: laya-rl-agent` for every checkpoint, so even `tune`'s check cannot tell Laya checkpoints apart. Check mechanism: CLI subprocess test (wiremock server A, record, switch `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` to server B, record again, assert the second run is refused or flagged).
2. **A CI gate that measures recordings, not the model.** `jud eval --replay` over committed recordings can only catch label or question edits and missing recordings (`run-in-ci.md` says exactly that). It never notices that `jev-latest` moved, that a server's `confidence` changed, or that the recordings are from a different model than production uses. The docs warn about the alias moving (`hosted-typesafe.md`, "What this does and does not establish"). Mitigation is not enforced: nothing records or compares the model's name against what the rubric's production backend will use. Related gate holes, read in code: no `--min-accuracy` means `jud eval` exits 0 whatever the accuracy (`eval.rs:1015-1033`); the bar compares a point estimate with no minimum count (`BarCheck::new`, `labelled` is reported but not a precondition, `eval.rs:353-365`), so one correct label meets 0.9; `--min-accuracy` holds the model's accuracy, not the policy's (`eval.rs:30`, docs say the same); `eval` does not call `warn_duplicates` (only `record.rs:385` and `tune.rs:91` do), so two recordings of one request leave `eval` reading the name-order-last one (`backend.rs:474-490`) without a word. The "nothing was measured" case is handled correctly (`checks`, `eval.rs:716-739`: an unlabelled question fails its bar), which I confirmed.
3. **Silent spend or silent wrong-model against the wrong server.** Mechanisms read in code: (a) a blank `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` falls through to the hosted default (`config.rs:env_var`); (b) the model can only be set in the file, so a user pointing `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` at Laya and forgetting `model:` sends `jev-latest`, which Laya routes by language to an on-demand base checkpoint instead of refusing (`laya-typed-decisions.md`), a 78 s first-call download in the recorded run; (c) autojev-serve accepts `jev-latest`, so recordings are labelled as Jev (`autojev-serve.md`, "Why the profile"); (d) plain `jud RUBRIC` prints no server banner, only `record`/`eval` do. `jud config` shows the resolved values but is a separate command nobody has to run.
4. **A recording that stops matching.** Mostly loud: a changed state or question text changes the fingerprint and the run exits 1 naming the cases (`batch.rs:answer_all`). Subtle cases: two files for one request make `Replay` choose by name order (`eval` does not warn); a recording whose request still matches but whose response no longer verifies is reported as "matches this state and rubric but cannot answer it" (`backend.rs:answer`); `request_hash` (FNV-1a, 64-bit) is the fallback for old `.json` recordings and is documented as not collision-resistant (`eval/mod.rs:209`). The option-order dependence matters here: `Questions` and options keep insertion order (CLAUDE.md), so a caller that builds options from an unordered map changes the fingerprint between runs (OpenHuman sorts alphabetically on its side, so it is stable but order-biased).
5. **A tuned threshold that is wrong.** Read in code: `jud tune` picks the lowest bar meeting the target over as few as 3 covered cases (`--min-covered` default 3, `tuning.rs:283-292`), on the same data it reports on unless the user ran `jud split`; confidence has different meanings per server (TypeSafe spread, Laya normalised entropy), and the hosted model's repeat-to-repeat spread is up to 0.28 on ambiguous input (`hosted-typesafe.md`), so a bar derived from one recorded draw can land on the wrong side on the next. `tune` refuses a mixed-model directory but not a model whose alias has since moved.
6. **A silent wrong answer from a 2xx.** The defences are real: `Response::verify` rejects off-list options, wrong primitives, wrong score scales (`answer.rs` module docs; every backend calls it). What it deliberately does not check: that the chosen option is the argmax, that distributions sum to 1, that a score equals the expectation, and answer-level extras are dropped. A server that returns a plausible distribution that is wrong is invisible by design.
7. **Billed failure with no usage report.** A 2xx that fails to decode is billed and `on_usage` is not called (section 1.1); a retried 5xx or timeout may be billed and is counted only as a failed attempt. The cost of a bad day is under-reported by the observer.
8. **Cold local server.** Laya first load (78 s) and Ollama first-model load exceed the 30 s `jud` timeout; the retry loop then repeats the request twice against a server that is still loading. The error surfaces as `Transport` or `Http`, with the retry count.

## 4. Where the OpenHuman caller stresses the integration points

(From the brief; not re-verified.) Tool options sorted alphabetically by a `BTreeMap` on its side means the model sees a fixed but order-biased list; thresholds hand-set with no calibration means failure modes 5 and 2 apply with no safety net; it likely uses the Rust API with one shared `Client` and the process-global observer, which is the section 1.1 observer caveat.

## 5. Candidate checks, by mechanism (no tests were run)

| Target | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Failure 1: record/replay across servers | CLI subprocess test with two wiremock servers (`tests/jud_record.rs` style) |
| Failure 2: gate holes (no bar, thin n, duplicates) | CLI subprocess tests on `jud eval` with crafted recordings and cases |
| Failure 3a: blank `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` | CLI subprocess test, assert which server receives the call |

## 2. Verification records: what real servers did that mocks did not

From `docs/project/verification/{hosted-typesafe,autojev-serve,laya-typed-decisions}.md`:

- Hosted API has three different 400 body shapes (a string `detail`, `{error_type, message}`, `{error_type}` with no message) and 422 with one issue per union alternative; the mock-era client assumed one. Fixed in `Error::InvalidRequest.kind`.
- Hosted API: `extra` top-level field gets a 400 `Invalid request.` naming no field; an extra field inside a question is silently ignored; duplicate question ids answered "last wins"; 40k-token state gives `max_tokens_exceeded` with no message; hosted answers are non-deterministic at the hundredths (spread grows with ambiguity), so a recording is one draw.
- Laya >=0.3.22 echoes structured levels as JSON text with Python spacing: `verify` refused every structured level (`4852f46`). Mocks written from the OpenAPI document could not show this.
- autojev-serve: 422 where the hosted API says 400, answers an empty question id under key `""`, no token budget check; the live-test profile mechanism (`JUDGMENT_LIVE_PROFILE`) was added because a model-name sniff misclassified it (`ce0a46b`).
- OpenRouter: base URL with a path was unreachable until `4f50bc8`; its 402 is documented for another API and "not yet seen" on System One (`7e27693` rewrote the docs to say so). Honest note: the OpenRouter 402 and body-id fallback are mock-tested only.

Lesson for property work: every wire-shape bug so far was found by running a **real server**, not by wiremock. A fake server that deliberately varies shape (a fault-injecting TCP shim already exists) is the cheapest way to get that class without a key.

---

## 3. The eight open beads, validated against the code

Standing of the source for all eight: single reporter ("Created by: Claude"), no comments, P3/P4, filed 2026-10-07/08 by an agent during review of the author's own work. Weak testimony by `validating-claims.md`; each is judged below on the code.

### `judgment-hle` (userinfo in base URL gives Basic auth, not Bearer): CONFIRMED by mechanism

- Competing explanation: the reporter's wiremock matcher or a proxy changed the header; the client's `default_headers` Bearer wins.
- Discriminating detail: `ClientBuilder::build` keeps `Url::parse` result with userinfo intact (`src/client.rs:452-459`, only the path is touched) and puts Bearer in the client-level `default_headers` (`src/client.rs:470-472`). reqwest 0.13.5 `RequestBuilder::new` (`src/async_impl/request.rs:171-183`) calls `extract_authority` (`:586-607`), strips the userinfo from the URL, and calls `basic_auth`, which does `header_sensitive(AUTHORIZATION, ...)` on the **request** headers. Request headers are set before client defaults are merged (client defaults only fill vacant entries; the `Entry` import at `client.rs:49` is that merge), so the request's Basic beats the default Bearer. I did not execute it, so the precedence step is read, not run.
- Extra finding: both `Debug` impls print the base URL raw (`src/client.rs:350` prints `self.base_url`; `src/client.rs:507` prints `self.base_url.as_str()`) while the key is `<redacted>`. A base URL with credentials appears in `{:?}` of the builder and client. The binary scrubs userinfo (`backend::public_url`, `src/bin/jud/backend.rs:188`); the library does not. Not in the bead.
- Property: for any base URL with userinfo, either `build()` is `Err` or the wire `Authorization` equals `Bearer <key>` (wiremock). A `Debug` property: formatted client never contains the userinfo.

### `judgment-smg` (empty `JUD_REPLAY=` refused by every command): CONFIRMED by mechanism, and already documented

- Competing explanation: clap treats an empty env var as unset. It does not.
- Discriminating detail: `replay` is `#[arg(long, env = "JUD_REPLAY")] Option<PathBuf>` on the top-level `Cli` (`src/bin/jud/main.rs:94`), and again on `eval` (`src/bin/jud/eval.rs:47`) and `tune` (`src/bin/jud/tune.rs:60`). clap_builder 4.6.7 stores `env::var_os` as `Some("")` (`builder/arg.rs:2207`), `add_env` feeds any `Some` value to `react` (`parser/parser.rs:1426-1438`), and `PathBufValueParser::parse` rejects an empty value with `Error::empty_value` (`builder/value_parser.rs:1022-1029`). Because `add_env` runs on the top-level command for every invocation, `jud check` fails too. `docs/reference/configuration.md:34` already states that an empty `JUD_REPLAY` "does not" count as unset. So it is a documented wart, not a surprise; the bead is a design decision.
- Not run, and no test exists for an empty value (`grep JUD_REPLAY tests/` shows only set-to-directory cases). Property: for every command, `JUD_REPLAY=""` and unset give the same exit status (this fails today by design).

### `judgment-3u8` (strict gates swept as if met at the bar): CONFIRMED

- Competing explanation: the sweep is intentionally non-strict and only the policy is strict, which is a documented difference, not a bug.
- Discriminating detail: `Rubric` acts on `value > bar` when `strict` (`src/jud/rubric.rs:184-186`, used at `:756` and `:764`), while `eval::tuning::gate_table` counts `*c >= bar` (`src/eval/tuning.rs:~262`) and `threshold_sweep` counts `*p >= threshold` (`:88`), with no strict parameter in either signature. So for a strict gate the printed row, coverage, F1 and the written note describe a different policy than the one written. Mitigation present: `note_strict` prints how many answers sit exactly at the bar (`src/bin/jud/tune.rs:299-300`, `:449-496`, tested by `a_strict_gate_names_the_answers_at_the_bar_it_would_defer`). Confidence values are 2-decimal wire values, so ties at 0.05-step bars are realistic (the bar grid is `i/20`, `default_bars` `src/eval/tuning.rs:63`). The defect is real; its severity is bounded by the stderr note.
- Property: for a strict gate, `covered(bar)` equals the number of judgments the policy actually acts on at that bar (differential test of table vs `Rubric::apply` over generated confidences that include exact-bar ties).

### `judgment-dtf` (Score table reads argmax, policy reads nearest level): CONFIRMED by reading, impact unquantified

- Competing explanation: the two readings coincide in practice. They do for one-peaked answers; the code comment says so (`src/bin/jud/tune.rs:~364`).
- Discriminating detail: `Judgment::new` sets `correct = (expected == predicted)` (`src/eval/mod.rs:298`), and for a Score the library's predicted is the most probable level (header comment, `src/bin/jud/eval.rs:~100`: "a Score by its most probable level"). The policy path uses `score.nearest_level()` (`src/jud/rubric.rs:793`), the level nearest the probability-weighted score. These differ on spread or bimodal distributions (e.g. p = [0.45, 0.10, 0.45] has argmax at an end, expected value at the middle). `gate_table`/`lowest_bar` consume `.correct` (`src/eval/tuning.rs:251-296`), so the proposed bar is justified by accuracy of a quantity the policy never emits. `level_sweep` already reads nearest level (`:175`), so the library has both readings; only the confidence table lacks one. A stderr note exists (`tune.rs` "the table reads the most probable level...").
- Unsettled: how often they differ on real model output (the live and recorded data would settle it; the `jud_calibration` recording could be scanned).
- Property: generate Score distributions; for the gate's own verdict compare `Verdict::Level.nearest` with `Judgment.predicted`, and assert the table's `correct` count equals the count of verdicts equal to the label.

### `judgment-bej` (propose nothing instead of confidence 0.0): CONFIRMED as a behaviour, a policy question rather than a defect

- Competing explanation: it is the documented rule of decision 0021 (lowest bar meeting target), not a bug. The bead says so itself ("changes the rule of decision 0021").
- Discriminating detail: `default_bars()` starts at 0.0 (`src/eval/tuning.rs:63`, "the first row ... is the baseline"); `lowest_bar` returns the minimum qualifying bar (`:283-296`); `tune_confidence` then sets `proposed.confidence = Some(row.bar)` even when `same(row.bar, 0.0)` and only prints the note "the proposed bar is 0, so the gate would defer nothing" (`src/bin/jud/tune.rs:370-376`, `:386`). So an author's `confidence: 0.3` becomes `0.0` and the written proposal removes a deferral that 6 labelled cases cannot justify removing (min_covered defaults small). The behaviour is real; whether it is wrong is a design choice. Safety angle: the proposal silently widens autonomous action.
- Property (if the rule is changed): tuning never lowers a bar to a value below the written one on fewer than N labelled cases; or, today: proposal==0 always accompanies the note.

### `judgment-rxl` (jud reads no `TYPESAFE_MODEL`): CONFIRMED, not a defect

- Discriminating detail: `grep TYPESAFE_MODEL src/` finds nothing; `READ_ENV = [API_KEY_ENV, BASE_URL_ENV, REPLAY_ENV]` (`src/bin/jud/config.rs:~22`), and the three-variable list drives the "ignored environment" warning, so `TYPESAFE_MODEL` is named as ignored on stderr and in `jud config` (`docs/reference/configuration.md:38`). The bead itself says "not a defect in either behaviour". No property applies beyond "an unread `TYPESAFE_*` variable is reported, never silently honoured".

### `judgment-3zp` (`jud tune --out` not atomic): CONFIRMED

- Discriminating detail: `std::fs::write(path, &yaml)` at `src/bin/jud/tune.rs:138`, a truncate-and-write; `record` uses `write_atomically` (temp file in same directory, `sync_all`, rename, remove on failure; `src/bin/jud/record.rs:620-632`). A crash or ENOSPC mid-write leaves a truncated rubric at the path. Mitigations: `check_out` refuses an `--out` that is an input, among recordings, or a hard/symlink to either (`tune.rs:172-200`), so the destroyed file can only be one the user just named, a lesser harm than the bead title suggests.
- Wider than the bead: the library's `eval::write_recording` (`src/eval/mod.rs:162-181`, used by `Recorder`, `src/backend.rs:385`) is also a plain `fs::write` after `create_dir_all`. A partial `.json` recording makes `Replay::open` fail with `InvalidRecording` for the whole directory. Neither path has a crash-injection test (grep: no `failpoint`, `kill`, `ENOSPC`, `/dev/full`). Also `write_atomically` has no directory fsync after rename (durability across power loss, not visibility), and its temp name is `.{name}.{pid}.tmp`, so two writers of the same name inside one process would collide (not reachable today: one runtime, sequential).
- Property: after a write interrupted at any byte, the destination is either absent/old or complete (needs a write-failure shim or a `/dev/full` target; today only `record` satisfies it).

### `judgment-6d1` (`jud eval --json` should count labels per outcome): REFUTED as stated; stale

- Competing explanation: the bead is current and eval reports only per-question `labelled`.
- Discriminating detail: `src/bin/jud/eval.rs:115-122` documents (and `:212-260` implements) `outcomes: [{outcome, level, labelled, predicted, correct}]` for every outcome a question offers, `majority`, and `signals` (`never_answered`, `collapsed`, ...), the doc stating "`labelled` and `predicted` each add up to the question's `labelled`". Commit `b4cf304` ("eval signals read from real answers", 2026-10-09) landed after the bead (2026-10-08). What is still absent: the per-outcome **case names** (`cases` list) and a text-report coverage block naming thin outcomes. So the bead's headline need (per-outcome count) is met; a residue (case lists) remains. It is a feature request and never a bug, so there is no property premise.

### Summary

| Bead | Verdict | Class | Needs property? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hle` | confirmed (read; precedence step not run) | library bug, credential handling | yes: wire header and Debug redaction |
| `smg` | confirmed, documented | CLI design wart | low: exit-status equivalence |
| `3u8` | confirmed, mitigated by stderr note | library bug | yes: table vs policy differential |
| `dtf` | confirmed in code, frequency unsettled | library bug | yes: same differential, Score generator |
| `bej` | confirmed behaviour, design question | policy | only if the rule changes |
| `rxl` | confirmed, not a defect | design | no |
| `3zp` | confirmed, wider than reported | CLI + library durability | yes: write-failure shim |
| `6d1` | refuted (stale), residue only | feature | no |

---

## 4. Existing test strategy

Counts (grep of `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `#[ignore]`): `tests/` 14.2k lines; `tests/client.rs` 56, `contract.rs` 13, `backend.rs` 16, `jud_record.rs` 42, `jud_tune.rs` 42, `jud_eval.rs` 44, `jud_cli.rs` 26, `jud_loop.rs` 12, `jud_split.rs` 9, `jud.rs` 10, `docs_examples.rs` 12, `spans.rs` 3, `observer.rs` 1, `live.rs` 16 (17 `#[ignore]`), `openapi_drift.rs` 1 (2 ignore). Unit tests in `src/`: about 190 (`answer.rs` 32, `rubric.rs` 20, `client.rs` 15, `question.rs` 10, ...). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs fmt, clippy, `cargo test --all-features`, minimal-feature check, the two quickstart examples, doc build, doc/llms/CLI-reference generator checks, `jud check` on examples, prek, cog, mkdocs. **Kani is not in CI and not in `mise run check`** (`mise.toml:125-128`, depends list; the five `cargo kani` lines are only in `mise run kani`).

### Coverage matrix

|---|---|---|---|
| wiremock, `tests/client.rs` (56 tests) | request shape; 4xx mapping (400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 413, 422); 429 with `Retry-After`/`-ms`; budget; 503 and 529; exhausted retries with attempt count; success in status set not resent; redirect refused (307, 302); header reserve/override; extra fields; timeouts; unknown answer kinds; `verify` rejections; request id (header, body, last attempt, span); OpenRouter body/cost/402; base-URL path | server is a canned response per test; time via `fast_retries` (small real sleeps, not a virtual clock); one request at a time | no 408/500/502/504 at wiremock level (only 429/503/529 appear as `ResponseTemplate`; `is_retryable` is unit-tested in `http.rs`); no concurrent calls on a shared `Client`; no random status/header sequences; no response of arbitrary JSON shape |

The shim is the cheapest place to add a fault-sequence property |
| `tests/contract.rs` (13) | every builder request and every `Fake`/recording response validated against the vendored OpenAPI document (`jsonschema`); schema examples decode; documented differences between crate and schema | schema is the oracle; the schema is lax on the cases that bit (structured levels, string `detail`) | it validates **fixed** examples and builder outputs, not generated ones; no differential "crate decodes what the schema allows" over generated documents |
| `Fake`, `Recorder`, `Replay`, `tests/backend.rs` (16) | typed answers; off-list option refusal; scripted answer of another kind; Replay prefers fingerprint; name-order read; unreadable `.json`; skip non-regular files; recordings decode and rewrite byte-for-byte | filesystem is a temp dir | no write failure, partial file or ENOSPC; no two `Recorder`s on one directory; no `&dyn SystemOne` shared across tasks |
| committed recordings (`examples/recordings/*`, six dirs) | decode, re-encode byte-identical, replay for their sample, conform to schema | recordings are one draw from the model (the verification page says answers vary at the hundredths) | replay is exact-fingerprint: no test of near-miss states |
| Kani (5 proofs) | `nearest_index` (`answer.rs:1940`), `delay_with` within policy (`http.rs:773`, stubbed `try_from_secs_f64`), `truncate_to` char boundary (`http.rs:820`, N=6), `bin_index`, `nearest_rank` (`metrics.rs:173,195`) | `unwind(8)`, `retry<=10`, byte arrays of 6, `-Z stubbing` | not in CI; nothing on parsing, `verify`, the `.jud` reader, canonical JSON, the sweeps, or the retry loop's control flow (async not modelled) |
| CLI subprocess (`jud_*.rs`, about 130 tests) | exit statuses, stderr text, closed stdout/stderr (`a_closed_stdout_never_panics...`), `record` input protection (symlink, hard link), stale twins, dry run, `--refresh`, tune proposals and strict notes, eval signals, split, conversations (`jud_loop`) | server is wiremock or `--replay`; `$HOME` is a temp dir | no two `jud record` processes on one directory; no `kill` mid-write; no SIGINT; no weird locale or very large inputs; no empty `JUD_REPLAY` |
| `.jud` reader (`tests/jud.rs`, `src/jud` units, 34 unit tests) | schema vs reader refuse the same documents (fixed list); round-trips; fingerprints; syntax error quotes no document text | JSON Schemas under `schemas/jud/` | no generated or fuzzed documents; no differential reader-vs-schema over a generator; no round-trip property `parse(to_yaml(x)) == x`; no YAML-bomb / depth test found |
| `docs_examples.rs` (12) | README, tutorial, guide blocks held to code and transcripts | binary transcripts | documentation fidelity only |
| `observer.rs`, `spans.rs` | `on_failed_attempt` for unfit/undecodable 200; span request id; unknown-answer warning once | a custom `tracing` layer | `set_global` is tested once, in its own target (process-global); no concurrent observers |
| `live.rs` (16 `#[ignore]`) | real servers by profile (typesafe, clef, openrouter, laya, ollama, autojev); every body validated against the OpenAPI document; non-determinism; confidence formulas | needs keys or servers; never in CI | the OpenRouter 402 path is unobserved |
| `openapi_drift.rs` | vendored document equals the live one | network | only the document, not behaviour |

### Explicit absences, each confirmed by grep

- Property-based tests: `grep -riE 'proptest|quickcheck|bolero|arbitrary'` over `Cargo.toml src tests mise.toml .github` returns nothing. Hand-written tables stand in (`src/http.rs:664-727` lists inf, NaN, 1e400, ...).
- Fuzzing: no `fuzz/` directory, no `cargo-fuzz`, `libfuzzer`, `afl`, `honggfuzz` references.
- Concurrency model checking: no `loom` or `shuttle`; `join_all`, `JoinSet`, `tokio::spawn`, `thread::scope` do not appear in `tests/` or `src/`. The only threads are the raw TCP server's. `Fake` holds `Mutex<Vec<Call>>` (`src/backend.rs:144`) and the observer is a `OnceLock` (`src/observer.rs:44`); nothing exercises either under concurrency. `Client` is `Clone`-able over a `reqwest::Client`, but no test shares one across tasks.
- Crash/IO fault injection: no `failpoint`, `ENOSPC`, `/dev/full`, `kill`; atomic-write behaviour is asserted only on the happy path.
- Mutation testing, `insta`/snapshot libraries, `turmoil`: none.
- Time: no `tokio::time::pause`; retry tests use small real sleeps (`fast_retries`), so wait arithmetic is checked by Kani and unit tables only, not on the loop.

### Where new property checks add value (and where they would duplicate)

Add value:

1. **Table-vs-policy differential** (`3u8`, `dtf`, `bej`): generate confidences, ties at the 0.05 grid, spread Score distributions; compare `gate_table`/`lowest_bar` with `Rubric::apply`. Today only fixed tables and stderr text are tested.
2. **Reader/writer/schema round-trip and differential** for `.jud` (the 0.5.1 cluster): `parse(to_yaml(r))` equivalence; reader and JSON Schema accept the same generated documents; canonical-JSON fingerprint invariance under key order and number spelling (already a unit test with fixed inputs).
3. **Hostile-server response property** over the client: arbitrary JSON bodies and header sets; invariant: result is `Ok(verified)` or a classified `Error`, never a panic, never a retry of a 2xx, nothing unbounded in messages/spans (`sanitize_server_str`), request id obeys one predicate.
4. **Fault-sequence property over the TCP shim**: sequences of {reset, truncate, hang, 429+Retry-After, 5xx, good} against `max_retries`, `budget`, `retry_after_max`; invariants: attempts <= `max_retries + 1`, total wait bounded, a billed success never re-sent, transport policy honoured. The shim and `fast_retries` exist; the sequencing does not.
5. **Write-interruption check** for `tune --out`, `eval::write_recording`/`Recorder` (durability gap `3zp`).
6. **Concurrency on a shared `Client`, `Fake`, `Recorder`, observer**: the one genuinely unexamined axis; a plain `tokio` test with N tasks (no loom needed for the first pass).
7. **Base-URL/credential invariants** (`hle`): wire `Authorization` and `Debug` redaction for generated base URLs.
8. **Put Kani in CI**: the five proofs have value only if they run; today a regression in `http.rs` arithmetic is caught by unit tests, not by the proof.

Would duplicate: `Retry-After` value parsing (table plus Kani already cover it), `nearest_index`/`bin_index`/`nearest_rank`/`truncate_to` bounds (Kani), exact error mapping per status (about 15 wiremock tests), `Fake`/`Replay` verification refusals (about 16 tests), CLI exit statuses and messages (about 130 tests), and documentation drift (`docs_examples.rs`).

## Open questions (not settled)

- `hle`: whether request-level Basic beats client default Bearer is read from reqwest source, not executed; one wiremock test (`Authorization` header seen by server) settles it.
- `dtf`: how often argmax and nearest-level differ on real Score output; scan `examples/recordings/jud_calibration`.
- `7e27693`: whether a non-ASCII control or bidi character in a body `id` reaches a span or recording; settled by a unit test on `usable_request_id`.
- Retry-After HTTP-date far-past/future arithmetic was not traced.
- Whether `tests/client.rs::a_base_url_path_is_kept...` also covers `list_models` (name only was read).

title: REF SUT report C: claimed guarantees and unproven assumptions
description:
# SUT discovery C: safety claims, liveness claims, unproven assumptions

Commit 56acead. Scope `src/`. Method: attention focuses 4, 5 and 11. Every "claim" below is a claim to test, never a verified fact. I read code at the cited lines. I ran no tests, per the brief.

Check mechanisms named: **K** = Kani proof (`#[kani::proof]`; five exist: `http.rs:773,820`, `answer.rs:1940`, `metrics.rs:173,195`), **PT** = property-based test (none exist, `proptest` not a dependency), **WM** = wiremock test, **RAW** = raw `TcpListener` shim (`tests/client.rs:635`), **FAKE** = `Fake` / recording replay, **CLI** = subprocess test (`tests/jud_*.rs`), **FUZZ** = fuzz target, **LIVE** = `tests/live.rs`.

Honest summary up front: this is a client library plus CLI, not a distributed system. Focus 5 (liveness) yields only bounded-time properties; there is no "eventually" over a cluster. Focus 4 yields a large, well-documented set of claims. Focus 11 yields about 20 concrete assumptions. Several are drift or tension between the docs and the code.

Lint posture (`Cargo.toml:256-270`, `clippy.toml`): `unsafe_code = forbid`, `clippy::all` and `pedantic` warn, `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` warn. `clippy.toml` only lists doc identifiers. `float_cmp` and `cast_*` are pedantic, so they warn, and the code silences them locally with `#[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]` etc. (`answer.rs:571`, `metrics.rs:5-9`, `backend.rs:~170`). No lint forbids `unwrap_or_default` or `let _ =`, so those patterns are not enforced against. Nothing in the repo enforces `panic = "abort"` or an overflow-checks profile (no `[profile]` section).

---

## Part 1. Claimed safety guarantees (focus 4)

### A. Wire, builder and answer checking

**S1. An off-list option is an error, never a default.**
- Source: `CLAUDE.md` ("An off-list option is an error, never a default"); `answer.rs:56` ("An off-list option is an error, never the no-match option ... nothing is snapped or clamped"); `docs/project/internals.md` "Checking the response".
- Code: `verify_answer`, `answer.rs:481-537`. The chosen key and every distribution key must be in `criteria`.
- Property: for any Choice question and any response (random JSON), `verify` is `Ok` iff the choice and all distribution keys are offered. Mechanism: PT, FAKE; WM exists for the client path (`tests/client.rs:1617`).
- Tension: `Choice<O>::from_answer` (`answer.rs:~690-715`) maps unknown keys to `UnknownOption`, but a typed `Choice<O>` handle is only safe if `O::ALL` equals the sent criteria. A handle obtained via `Questions::handle::<Choice<O>>(id)` (`question.rs:329`) checks only `kind()`, not the enum. A question added by `dynamic_choice` and read as `Choice<Dept>` is safe only through `from_key`. That is fine, but it is the one place "get cannot fail after verify" (S3) rests on a caller convention.

**S2. Every backend holds the response against the questions it sent.**
- Source: `CLAUDE.md`; `backend.rs:3-10` ("Every backend returns only a response that answers the questions it was given"); `lib.rs:20-23`.
- Code: Client (`client.rs:620`), Fake (`backend.rs:~320`), Recorder (`backend.rs:373`), Replay (`backend.rs:~517`) all call `verify`.
- Gap: the `SystemOne` trait cannot force it ("A backend written elsewhere must verify itself", `backend.rs:44`). A blanket `impl for &T / Arc<T> / Box<T>` forwards only.
- Property: for each of the four backends, any response that is returned satisfies `verify(questions)`. Mechanism: FAKE with PT-generated responses; WM for Client; raw recording files for Replay.

**S3. After `verify`, `Response::get` with a handle from the same questions cannot fail.**
- Source: `answer.rs:36-38`; `get` doc `answer.rs:~445` ("After `Response::verify`, it cannot fail").
- Code: Score `from_answer` parses legend keys (`answer.rs:~822`); `verify` requires keys exactly `"0".."n-1"` (`score_fits`, `answer.rs:538-577`). Choice typed path depends on S1's caveat.
- Property: for every verified response and every handle, `get` is `Ok`. Mechanism: PT.

**S4. Score scale: legend has exactly one entry per level, keys `"0".."n-1"`, string level echoed exactly, structured level as same value or parsing string, probability keys exactly decimal indices, score within `0..=n-1` (+1e-9), NaN excluded.**
- Source: `internals.md` "Checking the response"; `answer.rs:44-52`; module docs.
- Code: `score_fits`, `is_level_key`, `legend_matches`, `SCORE_EPSILON = 1e-9` (`answer.rs:83,572-577`).
- Property: PT over legend / key / score shapes (`"01"`, `"+1"`, `-0.0`, `NaN`, 9.000000001).
- Deliberately unchecked (not a claim): distribution sums, argmax = `choice`, score = Σ i·p_i, missing offered options, extra ids.

**S5. `Probability` and `Confidence` never hold a value outside `[0,1]`.**
- Source: README ("a probability is a probability"); `answer.rs:3-13`.
- Code: `Probability::new` (`answer.rs:99`), `#[serde(try_from = "f64")]`; `(0.0..=1.0).contains` is false for NaN, so NaN is refused.
- Caveat: the `Probability(f64)` tuple field is private but `unwrap_or(Probability(0.0))` (`answer.rs:867`) constructs it internally. `Answer::Score.score` is a raw `f64`, not a newtype. `Judgment` and `eval` carry raw `f64`.
- Property: for any JSON number (incl. `1e400` -> serde_json rejects, `-0.0`, `1.0000000000000002`), decode yields `Err` or in-range. Mechanism: PT; K feasible (trivial).

**S6. The builder refuses before sending what the server refuses: more than 255 options, fewer than 2 or more than 10 levels, empty or duplicate id, empty option key, null level, Noul with neither instructions nor criteria.**
- Source: `question.rs:19-31`, `internals.md` "The builder".
- Code: `validate_with` (`question.rs:380-432`), `insert` (`question.rs:343`).
- Claim detail "unique ids": the duplicate check is on the exact string. `Questions::add` of a `Question::Choice` built from a deserialised `Question` goes through `validate` as well (`push`).
- Property: `Questions` can never hold a state that `validate` would refuse (also after `serde::Deserialize`, if `Questions` implements it; I did not check). Mechanism: PT; `tests/contract.rs` pins bounds against OpenAPI.

**S7. `Questions` and a Choice's options keep insertion order.**
- Source: `CLAUDE.md`; `internals.md` "The builder" ("a sorted map would send them alphabetically").
- Code: `IndexMap` (`question.rs:32,211`). Wire serialisation in `client.rs` `Body`.
- Hidden risk: `serde_json::to_value` sorts object keys unless the `preserve_order` feature is enabled. `Cargo.toml:82` is `serde_json = "1"` with no feature, so any code path that goes through `serde_json::Value` loses order. `internals.md:156` says the client streams the request with `to_vec` over the struct (`client.rs:~586`) and the order is "witnessed by byte position in the serialised request". `request_hash` and `request_fingerprint` call `serde_json::to_value(questions)` (`eval/mod.rs:214`), which is fine since both sort anyway.
- Property: bytes sent have questions and options in insertion order for any permutation. Mechanism: WM body inspection, PT on permutations; CLI `jud lower` output. Note OpenHuman sorts on its own side (brief), which this does not cover.

**S8. Fingerprints are RFC 8785 canonical JSON, over `spec` only, stable for good.**
- Source: `CLAUDE.md`; `stability.md` "Fingerprints exclude the envelope and never change"; `canonical.rs:1-9`.
- Code: `canonical::write` (`canonical.rs:~52-93`): UTF-16 key sort, `ecmascript` number format, serde_json string escaping.
- Check mechanism: known vector in `tests/jud.rs`; PT against a reference JCS implementation (none vendored); the RFC 8785 test vectors would need importing.
- Concerns (see U-list, items U9, U10): integers beyond 2^53 are printed exactly (`write_number`, `canonical.rs:~96-100`), where RFC 8785 requires the IEEE-754 double rendering. NaN / Infinity cannot occur in `Value`.

**S9. A document survives a read and a write with fingerprints unchanged.**
- Source: `jud-format.md:404` ("so a document survives a read and a write with its fingerprints unchanged").
- Code: `Rubric::to_yaml`, `serde_saphyr::to_string` (`jud/mod.rs:361`).
- Property: for any parsed document, `parse(to_yaml(d))` has equal fingerprints. Mechanism: PT / FUZZ over YAML floats (`0.1`, `1e-7`, `0.30000000000000004`), large ints, unicode, anchors. Not tested for floats as far as I could see; `tune` writes thresholds computed as `f64` through this path.

**S10. "Nothing about any application goes in; generic."** Not a runtime property; skip.

### B. Client and retry loop

**S11. A 2xx is never retried, even when its status is listed.**
- Source: `http.rs:46-49`; `internals.md` "The retry loop"; `is_retryable` doc.
- Code: `is_retryable` rejects `is_success` (`http.rs:187`). Test `a_listed_success_is_never_retried` (`http.rs:603`).
- **Tension (lead, strong):** `send_with_retries` retries a *2xx whose body read fails* under `TransportRetry::Any` (`http.rs:345-353`: `BodyRead::Transport` branch, no status check). `tests/client.rs:627-628,701` pins this with a `200 OK` with `content-length: 100` and a short body, retried three times. The status was a success and the call was possibly billed, so a second paid call is possible. Docs say "a body cut short included" for `Any` and "a connection never made" for `BeforeSend`, so it is an intended trade, but the sentence "a 2xx is never retried" is literally false for the default policy. Property: under the default policy, a 2xx with a cut body causes N+1 sends (document it), and under `conservative()` exactly 1. Mechanism: RAW (exists). Open question O1.

**S12. A 2xx the client cannot use (`decode`, `unfit`) is never retried and is reported to the observer.**
- Source: `CLAUDE.md`; `client.rs:36-44`; `internals.md` status table; `observer.rs:25-30`.
- Code: `Reply::decode` (`client.rs:~688`) reports `decode`; `evaluate_with` reports usage then `unfit` (`client.rs:619-623`). The loop already returned on the 2xx.
- Property: for a 2xx with invalid JSON / unfit answer, exactly one HTTP request is made, observer sees one `decode`/`unfit` failure, and for `unfit` one `on_usage`. Mechanism: WM `expect(1)` + recording observer (partly exists: `tests/client.rs:1688`, `tests/observer.rs`).
- Note: `list_models` (`client.rs:~640`) also decodes through `Reply::decode`, so its decode failure is reported with service `typesafe`, which is the same label as the evaluate path.

**S13. Every HTTP call goes through `http::send_with_retries`.** `client.rs:~655` (`Client::send`), used by both endpoints. Property: a code-structure check (grep / architecture test: no `.send()` outside `http.rs`). Mechanism: static test.

**S14. The key is checked at build time; an explicit key is never replaced by the environment's; blank is `MissingApiKey`; whitespace/control/non-ASCII or non-UTF-8 env is `InvalidApiKey`; no message quotes any part of a key; the key is marked sensitive and redacted from `Debug`.**
- Source: `client.rs:15-20`; `error.rs:35-50`; `internals.md` "The client".
- Code: `ClientBuilder::build` (`client.rs:443-486`): `resolve_api_key`, `auth.set_sensitive(true)`; custom `Debug` (`client.rs:~498`).
- Gaps in the claim: (a) a server that echoes the `Authorization` header or key in an error body: `PermissionDenied.detail`, `Http.body`, `InvalidRequest.message` quote the server's text (`internals.md:39`, truncated to 2000 bytes, not scrubbed). The crate never quotes the key itself, but a proxy might. (b) `Client` is `Clone`; `Debug` redacts. (c) The CLI re-implements key reading in `config.rs:123` (`env_var`) and passes the result to `.api_key(...)`, so the "non-UTF-8 env is InvalidApiKey" rule does not apply to the CLI (see U12). (d) Open bead `judgment-hle` (base URL with userinfo makes the client send Basic auth instead of Bearer): the code does not strip userinfo (`client.rs:445`, `Url::parse` then only a path fix). Whether reqwest then sends `Authorization: Basic` over the default header, I have not verified. Open question O2.
- Property: for any key string and any server error body, no `Error` Display / Debug / span field contains the key as sent by the client (excluding a server echo). Mechanism: PT over key strings with WM that returns the request headers in the body (shows the echo exposure).

**S15. No redirect is followed.** `client.rs:476` `redirect::Policy::none()`; test `a_redirect_is_an_error_and_never_followed` (`tests/client.rs:1186`). Property (done by WM). Note the loop `make` is also used for `list_models` GET.

**S16. Reserved headers and body fields are refused, not overridden** (`authorization`, `content-type`, `user-agent`, `x-typesafe-retry-count`, `content-length`, `transfer-encoding`, `host`, `connection`, `te`, `upgrade`; `state`, `model`, `questions`). Source: `internals.md:43`; `client.rs:145-162`. Code: `refuse_reserved_header`, field refusal in `extra_field`. Property: PT over header name casings (`HeaderName` is case-folded), including builder defaults, call options. Gap: `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, `expect` are not reserved. Is `Expect: 100-continue` a hazard? Unknown; open question O3.

**S17. Retry-After is honoured only up to `retry_after_max`; above it the client's own backoff applies; a hostile header cannot stall a caller.**
- Source: `http.rs:50-57`; `internals.md:51`.
- Code: `delay_with` (`http.rs:207-231`); K proof `http.rs:820` (no panic, bound within cap).
- Note: "capped" is a misnomer; above the cap it is *replaced* by the backoff, not truncated. Test `retry_after_wins_when_within_cap` (`http.rs:508`).

**S18. Jitter is one-sided: delay never exceeds the nominal backoff.** Proven by K and unit test `jitter_only_subtracts`.

**S19. The budget never starts a wait that would end at or past it; an attempt in flight is never cut.** `next_wait` (`http.rs:235-258`). Test `budget_stops_before_a_wait_that_reaches_it`. Overrun bound: budget + one per-attempt timeout (documented).

**S20. The body cap (8 MiB): a `Content-Length` above it is refused before reading; otherwise chunk by chunk; over the cap is never retried.** `read_body` (`http.rs:405-419`). Gap: a 5xx with an over-cap body returns `TooLarge` (not retried) *before* the status is considered (`http.rs:330-344` precedes `:360`), so a retryable 503 with a big HTML page becomes `ResponseTooLarge`, non-retried. Documented as "never retried since the next attempt would carry the same body" (true only for a deterministic server). Open question O4.

**S21. Every failed attempt is reported to the global observer, retried or not.** `http.rs:327,333,346,381`. Gap: the first branch reports `on_failed_attempt(service, status.as_str())` for *every* non-2xx, including a 3xx with `redirect::none`, fine. A body-read failure on a 2xx is reported as `transport` (correct).

**S22. Token usage goes to the client's observer else the global; failed attempts always global; `set_global` is first-call-wins.** `observer.rs:44-60`, `client.rs:649-651`. Property: with two threads racing `set_global`, exactly one wins; `global()` always returns the winner. Mechanism: loom is feasible but `OnceLock` is std (trust). Process-global state makes tests order-dependent (`tests/observer.rs`).

**S23. Request-id: a value that is empty, not printable ASCII or longer than 256 bytes is ignored.** `internals.md:41`. Code: `usable_request_id` (`client.rs:926-935`) checks only `is_ascii_control` and length, so a **body** `id` containing non-ASCII Unicode (e.g. U+202E bidi override, zero-width) is accepted and logged and placed in a recording; the header path is stricter (`to_str().ok()?` fails on non-visible-ASCII). Docs drift. Property: PT over strings.

**S24. Every server-chosen string reaching a message, log line, span or graded judgment goes through `sanitize_server_str` (escape_debug, 64 chars).** Source: `internals.md:86`. Code: `answer.rs:251`. Gaps: HTTP error bodies use `truncate` (2000 bytes, no escape, `http.rs:466`); `Error::Http.body` holds control characters; the CLI re-escapes via `out::plain` (`out.rs:43`, controls only, not bidi format characters). Mechanism: grep-style audit plus PT of error Display for ESC bytes.

**S25. Errors are grouped by what fixes them** (`Error`). Doc claim; property is classification of status codes: 400/413/422 InvalidRequest, 401, 402, 403, 408 Http, 429 RateLimited, 529 Overloaded. `classify` (`client.rs:~718`). Mechanism: WM table test (exists `maps_4xx_by_remedy`); PT over all u16 statuses for "no panic, total".

### C. Backends, recordings, eval

**S26. `Recorder` verifies before writing, so a recording is only ever a response a replay can return.** `backend.rs:373-374`. Property holds if replay's questions equal the recorded questions. Caveat: the `Recorder` keys by `request_hash` (FNV) of state + questions; two different requests with an FNV collision overwrite each other's file. `Replay` verifies against the request's questions, so a colliding response for a different question set fails verify most of the time but a collision with identical ids and shapes returns the wrong answer. Documented as non-adversarial.

**S27. A recording is written whole or not at all.**
- Claimed for `jud record`: `cli.md` "Atomic", `record.rs:600-632` `write_atomically` (temp file in same dir, `sync_all`, rename, temp name `.NAME.PID.tmp`, never `.jud`/`.json`), decision 0021.
- **Not true for the library `write_recording` / `Recorder`** (`eval/mod.rs:164-170`): `std::fs::write(&path, ...)` truncates in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write leaves a truncated `.json`, and `Replay::open` refuses the *whole directory* on one unparsable file (`backend.rs:~455-467`, `InvalidRecording`). Concurrent `Recorder` calls for one request in one process write one path. Bead `judgment-3zp` is the same weakness for `tune --out` (`tune.rs:~118`, `std::fs::write`, confirmed). Property: kill a writer at every byte offset; reader sees either the old file, or the new, or absence. Mechanism: fault-injection shim over a temp dir (crash after N bytes), CLI subprocess kill (`SIGKILL` loop) for `jud record`.
- Also: no directory `fsync` after the rename (`record.rs:626`), so "the answers already paid for are on disk" (`record.rs:14-17`) is not guaranteed across power loss; only process crash.

**S28. None of the commands writes over a rubric or cases document; `jud tune --out` never writes among the recordings; `jud split` writes over no file.**
- Source: `stability.md:44`, `cli.md:755`, decision 0021, `record.rs:22`, `tune.rs:1-10`, `split.rs:8`.
- Code: `same_file` (`fsutil.rs:11-26`): equal path, `canonicalize` equal, or same inode (Unix). `check_out` (`tune.rs:~160`), `refuse_inputs` (`record.rs:~540`), `write_new` with `create_new` (`split.rs:208`).
- Caveats: time-of-check to time-of-use (check at start, write later; `tune` check precedes the whole run); `canonicalize` fails for non-existent paths so a dangling symlink to the input is handled only by `landing` (`tune.rs:210`, 40 links). Non-Unix has no inode test. `jud split`'s "writes over no file" holds via `create_new`; a pre-check `exists()` plus `create_new` is fine.
- Property: for any out path spelled via symlink / hard link / `./` / case variant (case-insensitive FS) / trailing slash, input bytes are unchanged after any exit status. Mechanism: CLI subprocess (exists in `tests/jud_record.rs:805,845,877`); extend to symlink-to-dangling and case-insensitive spellings.

**S29. `jud split` writes both halves or neither.** `split.rs:128-134` removes the first half if the second fails to be created. ## Part 2. Liveness guarantees (focus 5)

Say plainly: nothing here is "eventually" in the distributed sense. These are bounded-time and progress claims for one process.

| ID | Property | Claimed or implied | Source / code |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | A call returns within the retry/timeout budget: at most `(max_retries+1)` per-attempt timeouts plus waits | **Implied** ("the attempt count and the per-attempt timeout already bound a call", `http.rs:66-68`); the budget bound is **claimed** ("budget plus one per-attempt timeout", `http.rs:64`) | `send_with_retries` `http.rs:313-396` |
| L2 | Per-attempt timeout bounds a slow server (slow-loris) including the body | **Implied**. Client sets `reqwest::ClientBuilder::timeout` (`client.rs:475`) and per call `rb.timeout` (`client.rs:306`), reqwest's timeout covers connect through end of body | no test sends a trickling body; RAW shim can |
| L3 | A resumed `jud record` completes the remaining cases | **Claimed** ("so an interrupted run resumes", `cli.md:259,294`, `record.rs:14`) | `record_one` `record.rs:~389`, `Replay::open` on the directory |
| L4 | `jud tune` terminates; never calls the backend | **Implied** (finite loops over finite recordings; `landing` bounded at 40 links `tune.rs:210`) | `tune.rs`, `tuning.rs` sweeps |
| L5 | `Retry-After` is honoured but capped; a hostile header cannot stall a caller | **Claimed** (`http.rs:55-57`) | `delay_with`; K proof |
| L6 | A failing call stops a record/eval run at once | **Claimed** ("the next call would fail the same way", `record.rs:~380`, `batch.rs:~196-205`) | `answer_all` returns on first non-Missing failure |
| L7 | Under a replay, one run names every case with no recording (does not stop at the first) | **Claimed** (`batch.rs:~196`) | `answer_all` collects `Missing` |
| L8 | `jud` reads stdin to the end; empty / invalid input refused | **Claimed** (cli.md:77) | `run.rs:~50` `read_to_string(stdin)`, **no timeout** |
| L9 | Dropping the future cancels the call, a wait included | **Claimed** (`internals.md:55`; `http.rs:92`) | tokio `sleep` and reqwest futures are cancel-safe; unit-testable with `tokio::time::pause` |
| L10 | A transient failure does not fail the decision (README: "a transient failure does not fail the decision") | **Claimed** | true only within `max_retries=2` and a 10 s timeout; a persistent one surfaces after ~`3*10 + waits` |

Detail and gaps:

- **L1 bound, worked out.** Library defaults: `max_retries=2`, timeout 10 s, backoff 0.5 s / 1 s, `retry_after_max=30 s`. A server answering `429` with `Retry-After: 30` each time gives `3*10 s + 2*30 s = 90 s` worst case without a budget; with the CLI's 30 s timeout `3*30+60 = 150 s`. `max_retries` is a `u32` with no ceiling and `budget` defaults to `None`, so a caller policy `max_retries: u32::MAX` makes the loop unbounded while the server keeps returning 503 (each wait ≤ `backoff_max`). The docs bound the default only. Property: for any policy and any server schedule, wall time ≤ `(max_retries+1)*timeout + Σ waits`; with a budget, ≤ budget + timeout. Mechanism: tokio `start_paused` virtual clock with a fake transport is hard here because reqwest owns the socket; use RAW shim with a scripted schedule plus `tokio::time::pause` for waits only, or a loom-free model test on `next_wait` (pure, already unit tested).
- **L1 edge.** `Retry-After: 0` and `retry_after_max = 0`: a zero wait honoured (`http.rs:208-211`), immediate retries, still bounded by `max_retries`.
- **L2 edge.** `timeout_secs: 0` in `config.yaml` is accepted (`config.rs:153`, no validation) and becomes `Duration::from_secs(0)` per attempt; every call would time out at once (reqwest treats a zero timeout as expiring immediately; I have not run it). Open question O7. A very large `timeout_secs` (u64) is accepted as well.
- **L3 resume correctness conditions.** The claim holds if: (a) every file in `--out` parses (one bad `.jud` or `.json` refuses the whole directory with status 2, `record.rs:~590-607`; a half-written *non-atomic* file cannot appear from `jud record` itself, but a `.json` from the library `Recorder` in the same directory can); (b) the model and server are the same: **the fingerprint excludes the model** (`canonical.rs:36-37`) and `Replay::answer` ignores `_model` (`backend.rs:~519`), so a run resumed with another model / base URL silently *keeps* the first model's recordings as "answers" (`kept NAME`). `jud tune` refuses mixed models after the fact (`tune.rs` `single_model`), `jud eval --replay` does not mention it. Property: resume after kill at any point yields the same set of files as an uninterrupted run, provided the backend is deterministic and the same. Mechanism: CLI subprocess with a server that dies at call k (exists: `a_failing_call_stops_the_run_and_keeps_what_was_recorded`, `tests/jud_record.rs:342`), extend with `SIGKILL` at random offsets inside `write_atomically` and with two concurrent `jud record` on one directory (the temp name carries the PID so two processes do not interleave, but the last rename wins and both pay for the same request; PID collision across containers sharing a volume is possible).
- **L8.** `read_state` blocks forever on a terminal or a pipe that never closes; there is no timeout or size cap. Acceptable for a CLI; note it for the harness (always close stdin).
- **Not claimed anywhere:** an overall deadline for `jud record` / `jud eval` (sequential, one call at a time, each bounded by L1), recovery of an interrupted `jud tune --out` (non-atomic write, bead `3zp`), or any progress guarantee under a server that returns 2xx with a decodable but unfit body (fails the run at once, status 1).
